definition_zh: 骚扰；侵扰；不断烦扰；反复进攻骚扰；使疲惫不堪
definition_en: to trouble someone repeatedly, or to keep attacking an enemy with small raids
core_image: 一只狗被放出去，对猎物紧追不放地撕咬骚扰
scene: 办公室里，同一个号码每天打来十几个电话，接起来又只是沉默。The calls stopped being occasional and began to harass everyone at the front desk.
sceneCN: 这里 harass 是「骚扰；不断烦扰」（第 1 个义项：反复纠缠打扰某人）；句意：来电起初只是偶尔，后来开始不断骚扰前台的每个人。

pos.zh: 骚扰；侵扰；反复进攻骚扰

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，指「骚扰；烦扰」的行为
由动词加 -er 构成，指「骚扰者」
过去分词作形容词，指「疲惫不堪的；被烦扰的」
现在分词作形容词，指「令人烦扰的」

senses.title: To pester someone again and again
senses.definition: to trouble or annoy someone repeatedly, so that they cannot settle or rest
senses.definitionCN: 一而再地打扰或惹恼某人，使其无法安心休息
senses.example: Reporters waited outside and harassed her for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 记者在门外守候，缠了她三天。
senses.why: Old French harer meant to set a hunting dog on an animal, and the hound running after its prey is the repeated trouble.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 harer 指放猎狗去追咬猎物，猎犬紧追不放的画面就是「反复的麻烦」。

senses.title: Unwelcome conduct
senses.definition: to subject someone to behaviour they do not want, often of a persistent or offensive kind
senses.definitionCN: 使某人遭受其不想要的行为，通常是持续性的或令人反感的
senses.example: The policy says no worker may harass a colleague about their private life.
senses.exampleCN: 规定说任何员工都不得就私事骚扰同事。
senses.why: Persistent pursuit of a person, the dog chase made social, becomes a legal wrong when the behaviour is unwanted.
senses.whyCN: 持续追逐他人，也就是把「狗追猎物」搬到社会里，一旦行为不受欢迎，就成了一种法律上的过错。

senses.title: To raid and wear down
senses.definition: to make repeated small attacks on an enemy, or to trouble a place with constant raids
senses.definitionCN: 对敌人反复发起小规模攻击，或以不断的袭击扰乱某地
senses.example: Small bands harassed the column all night from the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 小股人马整夜从山上袭扰这支行军队伍。
senses.why: The same hound image returns in war: you do not kill the prey at once, you chase it until it is exhausted.
senses.whyCN: 同样的猎犬意象回到战场上：不必一次杀死猎物，只要追到它筋疲力尽即可。

senses.title: Repeated attacks of trouble
senses.definition: to cause repeated difficulty to a place or an activity, so that it cannot go smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 不断给某地或某项活动造成困难，使其无法顺利进行
senses.example: Bad weather harassed the construction work for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气一连几周不断干扰施工。
senses.why: The hunted quarry loses its footing when the ground itself is under attack, so weather and trouble in general can harass a task.
senses.whyCN: 猎物失去立足之地就不难被追垮；当目标不是人而是事情本身受攻扰时，天气与麻烦也能 harass 一项任务。

senses.title: Worn out by pressure
senses.definition: to leave someone tired and troubled after long or continual pressure
senses.definitionCN: 长时间或不断的压力使某人疲惫而心烦
senses.example: She looked harassed after a morning of complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 抱怨了一上午之后，她看上去疲惫不堪。
senses.why: After a long chase the prey simply stops running, and a person under endless trouble looks the same way.
senses.whyCN: 追逐太久，猎物干脆跑不动了；一个人被无休止的麻烦围困时，也是这副样子。

intro.en: Harass comes from French harasser, a hunting word. Its deeper origin is uncertain: the dictionary record allows no firm answer.
intro.cn: harass 来自法语 harasser，本是一个打猎用语；更早的来源不确定，词典学界至今没有定论。

items.en: French harasser meant to tire out an animal by long pursuit.
items.cn: 法语 harasser 意为长时间追逐使动物疲惫不堪。

items.en: Its base harer, to set a dog on an animal, is the hunting side of the story.
items.cn: 其词根 harer 意为放狗追咬猎物，这是「打猎」那一面的来源。

items.en: Some scholars link harass with harer, yet the older origin is uncertain and no single source is agreed.
items.cn: 有学者把 harass 与 harer 联系起来，但更早的来源不确定，学界并未取得一致。

items.en: English borrowed harass in hunting and military senses, then extended it to people.
items.cn: 英语借入 harass 时用于打猎与军事语境，后来才扩展到对「人」的打扰。

items.en: The word gained a legal sense in employment and conduct law.
items.cn: 这个词二十世纪进入到劳动与行为法规，多了法律含义。

note.en: Harass is compared with its own noun and with words that describe pestering, bullying, and assault.
note.cn: harass 一方面与本词族的名词、形容词对照，一方面与表示纠缠、欺凌、侵犯的动词对照。

entries.definition: the act of troubling someone repeatedly
entries.definitionCN: 骚扰；烦扰的行为

entries.definition: a person who troubles others persistently
entries.definitionCN: 骚扰者

entries.definition: an outward show of courage; the ending is similar only in spelling
entries.definitionCN: 虚张声势；只是词尾拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to annoy someone with repeated questions or requests
entries.definitionCN: 纠缠；不断烦扰

entries.definition: to frighten or hurt someone who is weaker
entries.definitionCN: 欺负；欺凌

entries.definition: to attack or interfere with someone in an offensive way
entries.definitionCN: 侵犯；猥亵

normalIntro.en: Harass is a hunting verb in English clothing: the same root gives the noun harassment, and the stress moves in British and American speech.
normalIntro.cn: harass 是一个披着英语外衣的打猎动词，它的名词形式是 harassment，而英式和美式的重音位置并不相同。

normal.en: British speakers stress the first syllable, American speakers often the second.
normal.cn: 英式把重音放在第一个音节，美式常放在第二个音节。

normal.en: The passive frame is common: be harassed by calls, problems, or questions.
normal.cn: 被动结构很常见：be harassed by 加来电、问题等。

normal.en: The noun harassment is fixed in workplace law as a legal term.
normal.cn: 名词 harassment 已成为劳动法里的固定的法律术语。

normal.en: The past participle harassed works as an adjective for someone worn out.
normal.cn: 过去分词 harassed 可以当形容词，形容人被弄得疲惫不堪。

normal.en: Contrast pester, which is milder, with harass, which suggests persistence and often harm.
normal.cn: 对比 pester（较轻微）与 harass（更强调持续，且常含伤害意图）。

abstract.en: Picture a hound let loose that will not stop chasing the same animal.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被放开的猎犬，一路死追同一只猎物。

abstract.en: Picture a phone on a desk that rings again the moment it is put down.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的电话刚挂断就又响起来。

abstract.en: Picture a small group of riders circling a long column until it cannot move.
abstract.cn: 想象一小队骑手绕着长长的队伍打转，直到对方动弹不得。

examples.en: Several colleagues harass the new intern with jokes he never asked for.
examples.cn: 几位同事总用他不想要的玩笑骚扰这名新实习生。

examples.en: The law protects staff from harassment of any kind.
examples.cn: 法律保护员工免受任何形式的骚扰。

examples.en: After two nights of alarms, the whole shift looked harassed.
examples.cn: 连响两晚警报之后，整个班次的人都显得疲惫不堪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈，拉死」：被缠到拉扯得筋疲力尽，就是被骚扰得受不了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 harasser（追猎使疲惫）← harer（放狗追咬）→ 英语 harass，核心义「紧追不放地扰」，从打猎、军事扩至日常骚扰与法律语境。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts from hunting and war, where pursuers chase a quarry until it is worn out, and then widens into everyday pestering, legal harassment, and the resulting tiredness.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词起于打猎与作战：追逐者一路追赶猎物直到它精疲力竭；此后扩展到日常的纠缠、法律上的骚扰，以及被烦扰到疲惫的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hound set loose on an animal and kept chasing it.
core.cn: 核心意象：放出猎犬，对猎物紧追不放。

branches.en: The chase itself is pestering someone without let up.
branches.cn: 追逐本身，就是一刻不停地缠着别人。

branches.en: The chase turned against people gives the legal sense of harassment.
branches.cn: 把追逐搬到人与人之间，就得到法律意义上的骚扰。

branches.en: The hunting chase returns literally in small military raids.
branches.cn: 打猎式的追逐在军事小规模袭击中直接重现。

branches.en: Both a raiding party and bad weather keep coming back to break things up.
branches.cn: 袭扰的小队和恶劣天气都是反复来袭，把事情搅乱。

branches.en: Repeated trouble finally leaves the person worn thin.
branches.cn: 反复的麻烦最后把人磨得筋疲力尽。

intro.en: Harass is a borrowing rather than a compound, so its family is mainly built with -ment, -er, -ing, and the past participle ending.
intro.cn: harass 是借词而非复合词，它的词族主要靠 -ment、-er、-ing 以及过去分词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Harass is traced to French hunting vocabulary, and no Latin source is certain.
latinIntro.cn: harass 可追溯到法语的打猎词汇，其拉丁语来源并不确定。

items.example: Harasser is the French verb behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: harasser 是英语 harass 背后的法语动词。

items.meaning: to set a dog on an animal
items.example: Harer gives the hunting picture of a dog set loose.
items.exampleCN: harer 提供「放出猎狗」的打猎画面。

items.example: Harass entered English with military and hunting senses.
items.exampleCN: harass 带着军事与打猎含义进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 把动词变成名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ment forms the action noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成表示行为的名词。

items.example: Harassment is a legal term in labour law.
items.exampleCN: harassment 是劳动法里的术语。

items.example: The suffix -er names the person who does it.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 指做出这个动作的人。

items.example: Harasser is the agent noun of the verb.
items.exampleCN: harasser 是这个动词的施动名词。

items.example: Harassed describes the target of the trouble.
items.exampleCN: harassed 描述被烦扰的一方。

items.example: Harassing calls continued all week.
items.exampleCN: 令人烦扰的电话持续了一整周。

definition_zh: 耐寒的；能吃苦的；坚韧的；强壮的；大胆的（古义）
definition_en: strong and able to survive difficult conditions, especially cold weather or hard work
core_image: 一株长在石缝里的松树，冬天落雪也照样绿着
scene: 高原上的菜地秋天就冻上了，主人只种最泼实的品种。In such a short season only the hardiest vegetables will survive the frost.
sceneCN: 这里 hardy 是「耐寒的；能耐受恶劣环境的」（第 1 个义项：植物能熬过严寒）；句意：在这么短的季节里，只有最耐寒的蔬菜才能熬过霜冻。

pos.zh: 耐寒的；能吃苦的；坚韧的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ness 构成，指「耐寒性；坚强耐劳」
由词根 hard 加 -en 构成，义为「使变硬；使变坚强」，与 hardy 同源旁支
由 hardy 加 -hood 构成，古义为「大胆；无畏」，今多写作 hardiness
固定词组，指「耐寒多年生植物」，也比喻长期存在的事物

senses.title: Able to survive the cold
senses.definition: of a plant, able to live through frost and hard winter weather without shelter
senses.definitionCN: 指植物在没有防护的情况下能熬过霜冻与严冬
senses.example: This hardy shrub keeps its leaves on the coldest slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 这丛耐寒灌木在最冷的山坡上也保持着叶子。
senses.why: English hard, firm or tough, plus the adjective ending -y, gives the basic sense of something strong enough to last.
senses.whyCN: 英语 hard（坚固）加形容词词尾 -y，就给出「结实到能撑住」的基本含义。

senses.title: Tough and able to cope
senses.definition: of a person or animal, strong and able to live and work in hard conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指人或动物强健，能在艰苦条件下生活劳作
senses.example: A hardy climbing team crossed the pass before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 一支能吃苦的登山队在天黑前翻过了山口。
senses.why: If the stem alone means tough, people and animals that live in hard places are the next natural bearers of the quality.
senses.whyCN: 既然词干本身就表示坚固，那么生活在艰苦环境里的人与动物，就是这种品质最自然的下一批承载者。

senses.title: Resilient spirit
senses.definition: remaining cheerful and determined when life is difficult or repeatedly disappointing
senses.definitionCN: 生活艰难或一再受挫时仍保有干劲与乐观
senses.example: Years of hard dairy farming had made her hardy but not hard.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的辛苦奶牛养殖让她变得坚韧，却没有变得冷酷。
senses.why: Endurance that keeps a body alive can also keep a temper steady, so the word reaches the spirit.
senses.whyCN: 让身体撑下来的耐力，也能让脾气不被磨垮，于是这个词延伸到了精神上。

senses.title: Long lasting in use
senses.definition: able to keep working or flowering for a long time under strain
senses.definitionCN: 在压力之下仍能长时间运转或持续开花
senses.example: The hardy jeep outlived three newer models on the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆皮实的吉普车在农场上比三辆新款车都经用。
senses.why: A thing that endures cold and hardship also endures use, so the sense spreads from living things to tools.
senses.whyCN: 能扛住寒冷与艰苦的东西，也扛得住使用，于是这层意思从活物蔓延到器物。

senses.title: Bold and daring
senses.definition: old and literary, meaning bold and willing to risk danger
senses.definitionCN: 古旧而带文学色彩，意为胆大、敢于冒险
senses.example: Hardy knights rode out to meet the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 胆大的骑士出城迎击劫掠者。
senses.why: Old French hardi meant bold, and books keep that daring sense alive for knights and sailors.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 hardi 意为大胆，书籍为骑士与水手保留了这个「勇猛」义。

intro.en: Hardy comes from Old French hardi, bold, which goes back to the German-style root for hard, and its deeper Indo-European source is uncertain.
intro.cn: hardy 来自古法语 hardi（大胆的），可追溯到日耳曼式的「坚硬」词根，更早的印欧语源不确定。

items.en: A reconstructed Frankish verb, usually written as hardjan, means to make hard.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构的法兰克语动词（常写作 hardjan），意为使变硬。

items.en: Old French hardi meant bold, hardy, or daring.
items.cn: 古法语 hardi 意为大胆的、英勇的。

items.en: English took the word as hardy, first in the sense of bold and daring.
items.cn: 英语借入时作 hardy，最初表示大胆、勇猛。

items.en: The sense shifted towards able to endure hardship and hard weather.
items.cn: 词义随后转向能够忍受艰苦与恶劣天气。

items.en: Horticulture fixed hardy as the standard word for cold resistant plants.
items.cn: 园艺学把 hardy 固定为「耐寒」的标准用词。

note.en: Hardy is compared with its hard family and with look-alike names, and then with words for strong and cold resistant.
note.cn: hardy 一方面与 hard 词族及形近词对照，一方面与表示强壮、耐寒的词对照。

entries.definition: firm to the touch, or difficult
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬的；困难的

entries.definition: the quality of being tough and able to endure
entries.definitionCN: 耐寒性；坚强的品质

entries.definition: scarcely; the ending is similar but the meaning is unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 几乎不；只是拼写相近，意思与 hardy 无关

entries.definition: strong and not easily damaged or defeated
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的；坚韧的

entries.definition: able to recover quickly from trouble
entries.definitionCN: 有恢复力的；适应力强的

entries.definition: able to withstand frost, used mostly of plants
entries.definitionCN: 抗霜冻的，多用于植物

normalIntro.en: Hardy is the adjective built on hard, and its family moves between bold and tough: Old French hardi first meant daring.
normalIntro.cn: hardy 是由 hard 生成的形容词，它的家族在「大胆」与「坚韧」之间移动：古法语 hardi 最早指胆大。

normal.en: Link hardy to hard and harden, three steps on the same family line.
normal.cn: 把 hardy 与 hard、harden 串起来，是同一词族上的三级台阶。

normal.en: The noun hardiness, not hardyness, is the correct spelling.
normal.cn: 名词拼作 hardiness，而不是 hardyness。

normal.en: Horticulture uses hardy plus a zone number to say a plant can take the cold.
normal.cn: 园艺上常用 hardy 加耐寒区编号，表示植物能扛住当地的寒冷。

normal.en: The comparative and superlative change y to i: hardier, hardiest.
normal.cn: 比较级和最高级把 y 变 i：hardier 与 hardiest。

normal.en: Contrast hardy with hard: hard is about firmness, hardy about endurance of hardship.
normal.cn: 对比 hardy 与 hard：hard 讲「坚硬、困难」，hardy 讲「能忍受艰苦」。

abstract.en: Picture a pine rooted in a crack of rock, snow on its branches and still green.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵松树扎根在岩缝里，枝上落雪仍一片青绿。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer carrying two buckets up a frozen lane in winter boots.
abstract.cn: 想象一个农民穿着冬靴，提着两桶水走上结冰的乡间小路。

abstract.en: Picture a young tree bent back by wind and rising again after each gust.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵小树被风吹弯，每阵风过后又直起腰来。

examples.en: Only hardy animals could live on the bare island through winter.
examples.cn: 只有耐得住的动物才能在这座光秃秃的岛上过冬。

examples.en: The mountain guides were hardy and never complained of the cold.
examples.cn: 几位高山向导都很能吃苦，从不抱怨寒冷。

examples.en: Farmers choose hardy varieties when the growing season is short.
examples.cn: 生长季节短的时候，农民会挑耐寒的品种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈弟」：哈，这个弟弟真够硬的，大冬天也光着脸在外面跑，耐冻；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 hardi（大胆的），源自法兰克语重构形式（一般认为意为「使变硬」）→ 英语 hardy，核心义「硬得住、扛得住」，由「胆大」转为「耐寒、能吃苦」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins in the idea of boldness, then shifts to the ability to endure: cold for plants, hardship for people, strain for things, and finally an old literary return to daring.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词最初表示大胆，随后转向「熬得住」：植物熬住寒冷，人熬住艰苦，器物熬住磨损，最后一层则回到古老的文学色彩「胆大」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small pine rooted in rock that stays green through snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：扎根石缝的小松，落雪仍青。

branches.en: The most concrete survival is a plant that lives through frost.
branches.cn: 最具体的「熬过去」，就是植物熬过霜冻。

branches.en: People and animals inherit the same endurance in hard places.
branches.cn: 人和动物在艰苦之地继承了同样的忍耐力。

branches.en: Endurance reaches inward, into spirit and temper.
branches.cn: 忍耐力向内延伸，进入精神与性情。

branches.en: Both a cold resistant plant and a durable vehicle keep going under pressure.
branches.cn: 耐寒植物与耐用车辆都是在压力下撑得住。

branches.en: The oldest sense of bold daring survives in literary and heroic use.
branches.cn: 最古老的「胆大」义留在文学与英雄叙事的用法里。

intro.en: Hardy belongs to the hard family, with -y marking the adjective and the noun hardiness formed in turn from hardy.
intro.cn: hardy 属于 hard 词族：-y 标示它是形容词，名词 hardiness 又由 hardy 再生成。

latinIntro.en: The word passed through Old French, whose hardi goes back to a Germanic root rather than to Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经由古法语而来，古法语 hardi 追溯到日耳曼词根，而不是拉丁语。

items.example: The reconstructed root hardjan underlies the French forms.
items.exampleCN: 重构词根 hardjan 是法语各形式的底层来源。

items.example: Old French hardi gave English hardy.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 hardi 产生了英语 hardy。

items.example: Hardy kept the bold sense for centuries before it turned to cold resistance.
items.exampleCN: hardy 在几个世纪里保留着「胆大」义，之后才转向「耐寒」。

items.example: The suffix -y marks hardy as an adjective of quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 hardy 标成表性质的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms hardiness from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 从词干造出 hardiness。

items.example: Hardiness is the standard word in planting guides.
items.exampleCN: hardiness 是种植指南里的标准用词。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -hood forms the older noun hardihood.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -hood 构成较老的词 hardihood。

items.example: Hardihood preserves the oldest sense of the word.
items.exampleCN: hardihood 保留了这个词最古老的义项。

items.example: Harden is the verb cousin of hardy.
items.exampleCN: harden 是 hardy 的动词表亲。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成动词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -en turns hard into harden.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -en 把 hard 变成 harden。

latinEntries.example: The French form came from Germanic speech, not from Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个法语形式来自日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

definition_zh: 唇裂；兔唇（旧称）；裂唇的
definition_en: an old name for a split in the upper lip present from birth
core_image: 上唇像兔子的上唇那样裂开一道口子
scene: 医生翻开旧病历，看到早年记录里写着这个如今已不再使用的词。The old medical file still records the split lip with the word harelip.
sceneCN: 这里 harelip 是「唇裂的旧称」（第 1 个义项：指先天性的唇裂）；句意：旧病历里仍用 harelip 这个词记录那道裂开的嘴唇。

pos.zh: 唇裂；兔唇（旧称，现已不宜使用）

derivatives.zh: harelip 加 -ed 构成，义为「唇裂的」，属旧用法
现代医学与正式场合的替代词，义为「唇裂」，已不取动物形象

senses.title: A split upper lip at birth
senses.definition: a split or gap in the upper lip that a person has from birth
senses.definitionCN: 先天性的上唇裂开或缺损
senses.example: Doctors once described the split lip as harelip.
senses.exampleCN: 医生过去把这种上唇开裂称作 harelip。
senses.why: The second part lip names the body part, and the first part hare gives the picture of a rabbit split lip, so the word names the condition by likeness.
senses.whyCN: 后半 lip 点明是嘴唇，前半 hare 提供兔子裂唇的画面，于是这个词用打比方的方式命名这种状况。

senses.title: A term that is now avoided
senses.titleCN: 已过时且不宜使用的说法
senses.definition: an old-fashioned word that medical writing now replaces with cleft lip
senses.definitionCN: 旧时的说法，医学写作如今改用 cleft lip 这一中性术语
senses.example: Modern clinics avoid the word harelip and say cleft lip instead.
senses.exampleCN: 现代诊所避免使用 harelip，而说 cleft lip。
senses.why: Because the word compares people to an animal, it sounds unkind today, so medicine moved to a neutral description that also names the cleft.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词把人比作动物，今天听起来不友善，医学界便改用同样点明裂口、但不带贬义的中性描述。

senses.title: The adjective use
senses.definition: used before a noun in old texts to describe a split lip, as in harelip operation
senses.definitionCN: 在旧文本中置于名词前形容裂唇，如 harelip operation 这样的组合
senses.example: The old journal lists a harelip operation that took place in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧期刊记载了村里做过的一次 harelip operation。
senses.why: English often puts a compound before a noun as a label, so the medical noun slipped into adjective position without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把复合词放在名词前当标签，所以这个医学名词原封不动地进入形容词位置。

intro.en: Harelip is an English compound of hare and lip, built on the likeness between a split upper lip and the split lip of a rabbit.
intro.cn: harelip 是 hare（野兔）与 lip（嘴唇）的英语复合词，依据是上唇裂口与兔子裂唇的相似。

items.en: Hara is the Old English word for the hare.
items.cn: 古英语 hara 意为「野兔」。

items.en: The now standard form hare appears with the hare family of words.
items.cn: 如今通用的 hare 一词出现在「野兔」这一词族中。

items.en: The compound hare and lip is recorded in early modern medical and popular writing, but the first date of use is uncertain.
items.cn: hare 与 lip 的复合形式见于近代早期的医学与通俗文字，但首次使用的年代来源不确定。

items.en: The spelling harelip settles and the word spreads in general medicine.
items.cn: harelip 的拼写逐步固定，并在普通医学中流传开来。

items.en: Related Germanic forms share an ancestor usually reconstructed as hase, though the exact reconstruction is debated.
items.cn: 日耳曼语同源形式共享一个祖先，一般认为可重构为 hase，但确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Clinical writing drops the compound in favour of cleft lip.
items.cn: 现代临床写作放弃这一复合词，改用 cleft lip。

note.en: Harelip sits beside hare and the lip group in form, and beside cleft lip and cleft palate in meaning.
note.cn: harelip 在形式上与 hare 及 lip 词族相邻，在意义上与 cleft lip、cleft palate 相邻。

entries.definition: an animal like a large rabbit with long ears
entries.definitionCN: 野兔，形似大兔、耳朵很长

entries.definition: a common misspelling that replaces hare with hair
entries.definitionCN: 常见误拼，把 hare 写成 hair，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a blue bell shaped wild flower
entries.definitionCN: 蓝铃花，一种钟形野花，与 harelip 共用 hare 这一成分

entries.definition: the standard neutral name for a split upper lip
entries.definitionCN: 唇裂的标准中性术语，现代替代 harelip 的说法

entries.definition: a split in the roof of the mouth present from birth
entries.definitionCN: 腭裂，先天性的口腔顶部开裂，常与唇裂同时出现

entries.definition: a clinical phrase for a split lip that avoids animal imagery
entries.definitionCN: 指唇裂的临床说法，不用动物作比

normalIntro.en: Harelip is a picture word: it takes the split lip of a hare and uses it as a label for a human condition.
normalIntro.cn: harelip 是一个画面词：它拿野兔裂开的嘴唇当标签，贴在人身上的某种状况上。

normal.en: The compound joins hare and lip, so the first half tells you what the lip is compared to.
normal.cn: 这个复合词由 hare 与 lip 拼成，前半部分告诉你嘴唇被比成了什么。

normal.en: The plural harelips is regular and adds only an s.
normal.cn: 复数形式 harelips 规则变化，只加一个 s。

normal.en: Medical writing now prefers cleft lip, which names the split directly instead of using an animal.
normal.cn: 医学写作如今更偏好 cleft lip，它直接点出裂口，而不用动物作比。

normal.en: Careful spelling keeps hare, not hair: a hair lip is simply a mistake.
normal.cn: 拼写要保住 hare 而不是 hair：写成 hair lip 只是拼写错误。

normal.en: Pair it with cleft palate, the closely related condition of the roof of the mouth.
normal.cn: 把它与 cleft palate 配对记忆，那是口腔顶部开裂的相关状况。

abstract.en: Picture a rabbit profile with its upper lip split in a neat line, and then imagine the same line on a newborn face.
abstract.cn: 想象一只兔子的侧脸，上唇裂成一条整齐的线，再把这根线移到新生儿的脸上。

abstract.en: Think of a file folder that has been closed and stamped obsolete, yet the old label is still readable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个已经归档、被盖上过时印章的文件夹，上面的旧标签却仍看得清。

abstract.en: See a clinic sign that once read harelip but has been repainted to read cleft lip.
abstract.cn: 想象诊所的一块牌子，原写 harelip，后来被重新刷成 cleft lip。

examples.en: The old textbook still uses the term harelip for the condition.
examples.cn: 那本旧教科书仍然用 harelip 指这种状况。

examples.en: Like the word harelip, many old medical names have been replaced by neutral terms.
examples.cn: 和 harelip 一样，许多旧的医学名称已被中性术语取代。

examples.en: Harelip describes a split in the upper lip that is present at birth.
examples.cn: harelip 描述的是出生时就存在的上唇裂口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿，裂噗」——上唇裂开的样子像兔子「咧」开的嘴，这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 hare（野兔）+ lip（嘴唇）复合而成，以兔子裂开的上唇作比，字面即「兔唇」；ha 系成分与古英语 hara（野兔）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Harelip begins as a plain descriptive name for a split upper lip, becomes a label that is now avoided, and also appears before nouns as an old adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: harelip 先是描述上唇裂口的直白名称，再成为今天被回避的标签，也能放在名词前作旧式形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an upper lip split like the lip of a hare.
core.cn: 核心意象：上唇像野兔的嘴唇那样裂开。

branches.en: The literal sense names the birth condition through animal likeness.
branches.cn: 字面义项借动物的相似来命名这种先天状况。

branches.en: Because the likeness is unkind, the word has become a term to avoid.
branches.cn: 正因为这种打比方不友善，这个词成了需要回避的说法。

branches.en: The noun is set before another noun to label an operation or repair.
branches.cn: 这个名词可置于另一名词前，标注手术或修补。

branches.en: The same descriptive name is both literal in old texts and avoided in modern ones.
branches.cn: 同一个描述性名称在旧文本里是字面意义，在现代文本里则被回避。

branches.en: A harelip operation targets the split lip that sense one names.
branches.cn: harelip operation 处理的正是第一个义项所指的那道裂唇。

intro.en: Harelip is built from two free English words, hare and lip, and its word family runs through compound words such as harebell.
intro.cn: harelip 由 hare 与 lip 两个自由英语词构成，它的词族沿着 harebell 这类复合词延伸。

latinIntro.en: The two parts are Germanic English words without direct Latin origin, so the scientific terms come from Latin separately.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是日耳曼来源的英语词，没有直接的拉丁语来源，因此科学术语另从拉丁语而来。

items.meaning: a large rabbit with long ears
items.example: Hare is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: hare 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.meaning: either of the two fleshy edges of the mouth
items.example: Lip is the second half and names the body part.
items.exampleCN: lip 是后半部分，点明身体部位。

items.meaning: a split upper lip at birth
items.example: Harelip joins the two words with no suffix.
items.exampleCN: harelip 直接把两个词连在一起，不加词尾。

items.meaning: more than one such split lip
items.example: Harelips is the regular plural.
items.exampleCN: harelips 是规则复数。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms hareliped, a rare adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成罕见的形容词 hareliped。

items.meaning: a blue bell shaped wild flower
items.example: Harebell shares the hare element.
items.exampleCN: harebell 与它共用 hare 这一成分。

items.example: Cleft replaces the hare comparison in clinical use.
items.exampleCN: 临床用法用 cleft 取代了跟兔子打比方的方式。

items.meaning: the neutral name for a split lip
items.example: Cleft lip is the modern replacement.
items.exampleCN: cleft lip 是现代替代说法。

items.meaning: an operation on a split upper lip
items.example: Harelip operation shows the attributive use.
items.exampleCN: harelip operation 展示了它的定语用法。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 裂开的（英语术语，非拉丁语）

definition_zh: 和声的；和谐的；谐波的；谐波（名词）；泛音
definition_en: relating to harmony in sound, or to the extra tones that sound with a basic note; also harmonious
core_image: 几根琴弦一起振动，高低不同的音正好合成一种悦耳的和声
scene: 乐队排练时，指挥说新加入的声部要让整段音乐听起来更和谐融洽。In the rehearsal the conductor said the new part should make the whole piece harmonic.
sceneCN: 这里 harmonic 是「和谐的、融洽的」（第 2 个义项：各部分协调相合）；句意：指挥说新声部应让整首曲子听起来更融洽。

derivatives.zh: harmonic 加 -ally 构成副词，义为「和谐地；按谐波方式」
harmonic 加 -s 构成名词，义为「谐波学；泛音」
harmonic 加 -ity 构成名词，义为「调和性；谐波性」
harmonic 加 -ist 构成名词，义为「口琴演奏者」，也见于谐波研究者

senses.title: To do with harmony in music
senses.definition: relating to the chords and note combinations that make harmony in music
senses.definitionCN: 与音乐中和弦及音的组合形成和声有关的
senses.example: The students studied harmonic analysis of the chorale.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们研习了这首合唱曲的和声分析。
senses.why: The Greek root harmonia means a joint or fitting together, so harmonic first names notes fitted together in a chord.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 harmonia 意为「接合、嵌合」，所以 harmonic 最初指在和弦中彼此嵌合的音。

senses.title: Pleasing and in agreement
senses.definition: forming a pleasing or well balanced whole
senses.definitionCN: 构成悦目悦耳或协调统一的整体
senses.example: The garden has a harmonic balance of colour and shape.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园的色彩与形状有一种和谐的平衡。
senses.why: From fitted together notes the word widens to anything whose parts agree, since a pleasing chord is the model for agreement.
senses.whyCN: 从彼此嵌合的音，这个词扩展到任何各部分相合的事物，因为悦耳的和弦正是「相合」的范本。

senses.title: An overtone of a basic note
senses.definition: a tone whose frequency is a whole number multiple of a basic frequency
senses.definitionCN: 频率为基础频率整数倍的音
senses.example: A string gives a series of harmonics above its main note.
senses.exampleCN: 一根弦在主音之上发出一系列泛音。
senses.why: Physics shows that a struck string vibrates at whole number multiples, and those simple ratios are the very ratios that make harmony, so the extras are called harmonics.
senses.whyCN: 物理告诉我们，被拨动的弦按整数倍频率振动，而这些简单比例正是构成和声的比例，于是这些附带的音被称为谐波。

senses.title: A regular repeating motion
senses.definition: describing a back and forth motion that repeats in the simplest regular way
senses.definitionCN: 形容以最简单的规则方式往复重复的运动
senses.example: The pendulum follows simple harmonic motion when the swing is small.
senses.exampleCN: 当摆幅很小时，单摆作简谐运动。
senses.why: A pendulum swing traces the same smooth wave as a sound wave, so the tidy repeated vibration borrows the name of the musical wave.
senses.whyCN: 单摆的摆动画出与声波相同的平滑波形，于是这种规则的重复振动借用了音乐波形的名称。

senses.title: A special average in mathematics
senses.definition: relating to a mean found by averaging the reciprocals of a set of values
senses.definitionCN: 指由一组数值的倒数求平均所得的均值的
senses.example: The speed of the whole trip is the harmonic mean of the two speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 整段行程的速度是两种速度的调和平均数。
senses.why: Mathematicians of the Pythagorean school found these numbers in the lengths of strings that sound well together, so the arithmetic kept the name of the musical agreement.
senses.whyCN: 毕达哥拉斯学派在音高相合的弦长中发现这类数，于是数学沿用「音乐上的和谐」这个名称。

intro.en: Harmonic comes from Latin harmonicus and Greek harmonikos, from harmonia, a joining together, a name that music gave to math and science in turn.
intro.cn: harmonic 来自拉丁语 harmonicus 与希腊语 harmonikos，源于 harmonia（接合、和合），这个名字由音乐出发，随后进入数学与科学。

items.en: Harmonia means a fitting together, as of joints or of sounds.
items.cn: harmonia 意为接合、和合，可用于木工的榫接，也可用于音的组合。

items.en: Harmonikos describes a person or thing skilled at this fitting together.
items.cn: harmonikos 形容擅长这种接合的人或事物。

items.en: Latin borrows harmonicus from the Greek adjective.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语形容词借来 harmonicus。

items.en: Harmonic enters English through Latin and is first recorded in music, though the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: harmonic 经拉丁语进入英语，最早见于音乐领域，具体的首见年代来源不确定。

items.en: Acoustics and mathematics extend harmonic to overtones, waves, means and motions.
items.cn: 声学与数学把 harmonic 扩展到泛音、波、平均值与运动等概念。

items.en: The everyday sense of pleasing and in agreement keeps the old picture of parts fitting together.
items.cn: 现代英语里「和谐、融洽」的日常义项仍保留着「各部分互相嵌合」的旧画面。

note.en: Harmonic belongs to the harmony word family, next to harmonic and harmonics on the sound side and to melodic and rhythmic on the musical side.
note.cn: harmonic 属于 harmony 词族，在声音一侧与 harmonic、harmonics 相邻，在音乐一侧与 melodic、rhythmic 相邻。

entries.definition: the pleasing combination of notes or of parts
entries.definitionCN: 和声；和谐，与 harmonic 同词族

entries.definition: to make things agree or fit together
entries.definitionCN: 使一致；配和声

entries.definition: the study of musical tones or their overtones
entries.definitionCN: 谐波学；泛音，由 harmonic 加 -s 构成

entries.definition: relating to tune played in a single line
entries.definitionCN: 旋律的，与和声的纵向组合相对

entries.definition: relating to a pattern of beats
entries.definitionCN: 节奏的，与 harmonic 同属音乐术语

entries.definition: a weaker higher tone that sounds along with a note
entries.definitionCN: 泛音，即基音之外同时响起的较高弱的音

normalIntro.en: Harmonic carries the whole harmony family: notes fitted together, strings sounding in simple ratios, and waves that repeat in step.
normalIntro.cn: harmonic 承载着整个 harmony 词族：彼此嵌合的音、按简单比例共鸣的弦、以及步调一致的波形。

normal.en: Harmonic shares its root with harmony and harmonize, so the -ic ending turns the noun of agreement into an adjective.
normal.cn: harmonic 与 harmony、harmonize 同根，词尾 -ic 把表示「和合」的名词变成形容词。

normal.en: Simple harmonic motion is the pattern of a swinging pendulum, a standard phrase in physics.
normal.cn: simple harmonic motion 即单摆往复的样式，是物理教科书的标配短语。

normal.en: In electronics a harmonic is a wave at a whole number multiple of the base frequency.
normal.cn: 在电子学中，harmonic 指频率是基频整数倍的波。

normal.en: The harmonic series lists the overtones above a note, and musicians use it to tune instruments.
normal.cn: harmonic series 指一个音之上的泛音列，乐手用它调音。

normal.en: Compare harmonious, which uses -ious instead of -ic and describes the pleasing result rather than the musical relation.
normal.cn: 对比 harmonious：它用 -ious 而非 -ic，更多形容令人愉悦的结果，而非音乐中的关系。

abstract.en: Picture four strings plucked at once, each vibration a whole number multiple of the lowest, locking together into one rich sound.
abstract.cn: 想象四根弦同时拨响，每根弦的振动都是最低音的整数倍，彼此锁合成一个丰满的声音。

abstract.en: See a group of dancers who each keep their own step but land together on the same beat.
abstract.cn: 想象一群舞者各走各的步，却在同一个节拍上同时落脚。

abstract.en: Watch a playground swing go back and forth at the same unhurried pace, tracing the same arc every time.
abstract.cn: 看秋千以同样从容的节奏来回摆，每次都画出同一道弧线。

examples.en: The engineer measured the harmonic distortion of the signal.
examples.cn: 工程师测量了信号的谐波失真。

examples.en: A spring with a small weight shows simple harmonic motion.
examples.cn: 挂重量很小的弹簧表现为简谐运动。

examples.en: Her voice blended into a harmonic whole with the other singers.
examples.cn: 她的声音与其他歌者融成一个和谐的整体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈莫尼克」——「哈」一声唱出去，几个音「么」搭在一起就成和声；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 harmonia（接合、和合）→ harmonikos → 拉丁语 harmonicus → 英语 harmonic，核心义「音与音彼此嵌合」，由此分入音乐、物理与数学。

sensesIntro.en: Harmonic starts from chords fitted together, widens to anything pleasingly in agreement, and then serves for overtones, repeating motion and two kinds of mathematical mean.
sensesIntro.cn: harmonic 从彼此嵌合的和弦出发，扩展到任何协调相合的事物，再用于泛音、往复运动以及两种数学平均值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several strings sounding at once that fit together into one chord.
core.cn: 核心意象：几根弦同时鸣响，彼此嵌合成一个和弦。

branches.en: The musical sense names notes fitted together into chords.
branches.cn: 音乐义项指彼此嵌合成和弦的音。

branches.en: The everyday sense extends the same fitting together to anything in agreement.
branches.cn: 日常义项把同样的「嵌合」扩展到任何协调一致的事物。

branches.en: Overtones and repeating waves both rest on whole number ratios of vibration.
branches.cn: 泛音与往复波都建立在整数倍的振动比例上。

branches.en: The mathematical mean keeps the ancient link between number and musical agreement.
branches.cn: 数学里的调和平均保留着数字与音乐和合的古老联系。

branches.en: A harmonic in sound is literally the overtone of the note you hear.
branches.cn: 声音意义上的谐波，实际上就是你听到的那个音的泛音。

intro.en: Harmonic is the adjective of the harmony family, with the Greek suffix -ic, and from it come harmonically, harmonicity and harmonics.
intro.cn: harmonic 是 harmony 词族的形容词，带希腊语词尾 -ic，由它派生出 harmonically、harmonicity 与 harmonics。

latinIntro.en: The root harmonia means a joining, and Latin harmonicus carries the adjective into Europe.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 harmonia 意为接合，拉丁语 harmonicus 把这一形容词带入欧洲各语言。

items.meaning: a fitting together, agreement of sounds
items.example: Harmonia gives the core of agreement.
items.exampleCN: harmonia 提供「和合」这一核心。

items.example: Harmonikos is the direct model for the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: harmonikos 是英语形容词的直接范本。

items.example: Harmonicus passes the word to Latin.
items.exampleCN: harmonicus 把词传给拉丁语。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes an adjective from a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把名词变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 学科名词词尾或复数词尾
items.example: The suffix -s forms the name of the field, harmonics.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成学科名称 harmonics。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms harmonically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 harmonically。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms harmonicity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 harmonicity。

items.meaningCN: 从事某行业的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ist forms harmonicist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 harmonicist。

items.example: Harmonics is studied in acoustics.
items.exampleCN: harmonics 是声学中的课题。

definition_zh: 口琴；谐波音（旧义）；玻璃琴（旧义）
definition_en: a small hand held wind instrument played by blowing and drawing air through metal reeds
core_image: 手掌捧着一个细长小盒子，对着它的孔一格来回吹吸，盒子便发出和声般的音
scene: 旅行的人坐在火车窗边，从口袋里掏出那个能吹出整段旋律的小乐器。On the train a traveller took a small harmonica out of his pocket.
sceneCN: 这里 harmonica 是「口琴」（第 1 个义项：靠吹吸金属簧片发声的小乐器）；句意：火车上，一位旅客从口袋里掏出一把小口琴。

derivatives.zh: harmonic 去掉阴性的 -a 词尾回到形容词，义为「和声的；谐波的」，是 harmonica 的词源近亲
由 harmony 加 -ist 构成，义为「和声学家；擅长和声者」，与本词同属和声词族
由 harmony 加 -ize 构成，义为「配和声；使协调」

senses.title: The small mouth played reed instrument
senses.definition: a small flat wind instrument held in the hands and played by blowing and drawing air through a row of metal reeds
senses.definitionCN: 一种小巧扁平的吹奏乐器，用手捧着，靠对一排金属簧片吹气与吸气发声
senses.example: He always carries a harmonica in his coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他外套口袋里总揣着一只口琴。
senses.why: The name was given because the reeds of such an instrument together produce blended tones like a harmony, so the word for agreement became the name of the box.
senses.whyCN: 这类乐器的簧片合在一起能发出像是和声的混合音，于是表示「和合」的词就成了这只小盒子的名字。

senses.title: The old sense of a harmonic tone
senses.definition: an outdated name for a tone that sounds with another tone at a whole number ratio
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对与另一音按整数比同时发声的音的称呼
senses.example: Early acoustic papers used harmonica for a ringing overtone.
senses.exampleCN: 早期声学论文用 harmonica 指鸣响的泛音。
senses.why: Before the instrument sense became common, the Latin feminine noun harmonica named something harmonious in sound, including pure mathematical overtones.
senses.whyCN: 在「乐器」义流行之前，拉丁语阴性名词 harmonica 泛指声音上和合之物，也包括纯数学意义上的泛音。

senses.title: The glass harmonica
senses.definition: an instrument of tuned glass bowls that ring when rubbed with wet fingers
senses.definitionCN: 由成套定音玻璃碗组成、用湿手指摩擦而鸣响的乐器
senses.example: A thin ringing sound from the glass harmonica filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃琴细亮的鸣响充满了大厅。
senses.why: Benjamin Franklin named his rubbing glass instrument after the Italian word armonica, and English took the same name, which is also called the glass harmonica.
senses.whyCN: 本杰明·富兰克林把他发明的摩擦玻璃乐器依意大利语 armonica 命名，英语沿用同一名称，又称 glass harmonica。

intro.en: Harmonica comes from Latin harmonica, itself from Greek harmonikos, a thing belonging to harmony; the musical name was later given to the little reed instrument.
intro.cn: harmonica 来自拉丁语 harmonica，其源为希腊语 harmonikos，意为「属于和合的」；这个词后来被用来称呼那种小簧片乐器。

items.en: Harmonia is a joining together, and harmonika names things that belong to it.
items.cn: harmonia 意为接合、和合，harmonika 指属于和合的事物。

items.en: Harmonica is the Latin feminine form of harmonicus.
items.cn: harmonica 是拉丁语中 harmonicus 的阴性形式。

items.en: English uses harmonica, often in Greek phrases, mainly for the science of musical sounds.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪的希腊语短语中常用 harmonica，主要与音律学相关。

items.en: Franklin invents an instrument of rubbed glass and calls it the armonica, which English writers call the glass harmonica.
items.cn: 富兰克林于一七六二年发明摩擦玻璃乐器并命名为 armonica，英语作者称之为 glass harmonica。

items.en: The word usually means the mouth organ once that instrument spread in Europe and America.
items.cn: 随着这种乐器在欧美流行，harmonica 通常指的就是口琴。

items.en: Early trading names for the mouth organ include Mundharmonika, and German usage may have pushed the English name, though this is not certain.
items.cn: 这种乐器早期的一种商品名为 Mundharmonika，德语用法可能推动了英语名称，但此说并不确定。

note.en: Harmonica is a harmony family word that turned into an instrument name, so it sits next to harmonic and harmonics in form and next to mouth organ and French harp in meaning.
note.cn: harmonica 是由和声词族转为乐器名的词，形式上与 harmonic、harmonics 相邻，意义上与 mouth organ、French harp 相邻。

entries.definition: relating to harmony or to overtones
entries.definitionCN: 和声的；谐波的，与 harmonica 同根

entries.definition: the study of musical tones and their overtones
entries.definitionCN: 谐波学；泛音体系，只差末尾一个字母

entries.definition: forming a pleasing whole
entries.definitionCN: 和谐的，属同一词族

entries.definition: another common name for the same small reed instrument
entries.definitionCN: 口琴的另一种常见叫法

entries.definition: an American regional name for the harmonica
entries.definitionCN: 美国某些地区对口琴的称法

entries.definition: a joking blues name for the metal harmonica plates
entries.definitionCN: 布鲁斯乐手对金属簧片口琴的戏称

normalIntro.en: Harmonica is the harmony family wearing an -a ending, so the mouth organ and the science of overtones share one history.
normalIntro.cn: harmonica 是和声词族换上一个 -a 词尾的结果，于是口琴与泛音学共享同一段历史。

normal.en: The word is close to harmonic and harmonics, the instruments being named for the harmony produced by its reeds.
normal.cn: 这个词与 harmonic、harmonics 很接近，乐器正是以其簧片产生的和声得名。

normal.en: The phrases play the harmonica and blow on the harmonica are standard, and the plural is harmonicas.
normal.cn: play the harmonica 与 blow on the harmonica 都是标准说法，复数写作 harmonicas。

normal.en: The harmonica is a reed instrument, so air is drawn inward as well as blown out.
normal.cn: 口琴是簧片乐器，所以既要吹气也要吸气。

normal.en: Blues and folk music made the harmonica famous, and the ten hole version is often called the blues harp.
normal.cn: 布鲁斯与民谣让口琴名声大振，十孔款常被称为 blues harp。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with the glass harmonica, which is played by rubbing its rim with wet fingers.
normal.cn: 不要与 glass harmonica 混淆，那种乐器是用湿手指摩擦边缘发声的。

abstract.en: Picture a flat metal sandwich in a cupped hand, the player pulling air in and pushing it out so the two rows of reeds sing together.
abstract.cn: 想象一只扁平金属小方盒被双掌捧住，吹奏者一吸一吹，让两排簧片齐声歌唱。

abstract.en: See an old physics notebook where one column of numbers, a pure ratio, is simply labelled harmonica.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧物理笔记，其中一列按纯整数比的数字边上只标着 harmonica。

abstract.en: Think of a ring of wet glass rims turning under fingertips, each one humming a clear ringing note.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈湿漉漉的玻璃边缘在指尖下转动，每一片都嗡嗡地发出清亮的鸣响。

examples.en: She learned to play the harmonica by ear as a child.
examples.cn: 她小时候靠听就学会了吹口琴。

examples.en: The band added a harmonica solo at the end of the song.
examples.cn: 乐队在歌的结尾加了一段口琴独奏。

examples.en: Two harmonicas and a guitar were all the buskers needed.
examples.cn: 街头艺人们只需要两把口琴和一把吉他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈莫尼卡」——「哈莫尼」就是和声，「卡」一声，一张会唱和声的小卡片被捧在手里吹；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 harmonia（接合、和合）→ harmonikos → 拉丁语阴性形式 harmonica → 英语 harmonica；本义「和合之物」，先后指泛音、玻璃琴，最终指以簧片发出和声的口琴。

sensesIntro.en: Harmonica names first a small hand held instrument, then keeps an old technical sense of a pure overtone tone, and also survives in the name of Franklin and the glass instrument.
sensesIntro.cn: harmonica 首先指一种手持小乐器，其次保留了纯泛音的旧技术义，还留在富兰克林与玻璃琴的名称里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small box cupped in the hands, whose reeds blend into one harmony when you blow and draw.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被双掌捧住的小盒子，吹吸时簧片合成了同一个和声。

branches.en: The main sense is the mouth organ, named for the harmony of its reeds.
branches.cn: 主要义项是口琴，因其簧片和声而得名。

branches.en: An older technical sense kept the name for a pure overtone tone.
branches.cn: 较旧的技术义项把这个名字留给了纯泛音。

branches.en: The glass harmonica keeps the name in a different instrument.
branches.cn: 玻璃琴这个词组把这一名字留在了另一种乐器上。

branches.en: Both instruments are named for their smooth blended tones.
branches.cn: 两种乐器都因为音色平滑融合而得名。

branches.en: A ringing glass rim and a mathematical overtone are both pure, steady tones.
branches.cn: 玻璃边缘的鸣响与数学上的泛音都是纯净而稳定的音。

intro.en: Harmonica is the Latin feminine of harmonicus, and its family includes harmonic, harmonica, harmonics and the verb harmonize.
intro.cn: harmonica 是拉丁语 harmonicus 的阴性形式，其词族包括 harmonic、harmonica、harmonics 以及动词 harmonize。

latinIntro.en: The family starts from Greek harmonia, and Latin harmonica gives the word its final shape.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族始于希腊语 harmonia，拉丁语 harmonica 则给出它最终的样子。

items.example: Harmonia is the oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: harmonia 是词族里最古老的成员。

items.example: Harmonikos gives the shape of the adjectives.
items.exampleCN: harmonikos 给出形容词的形态。

items.example: Harmonica enters English as a learned term.
items.exampleCN: harmonica 作为学术用语进入英语。

items.example: The ending -a marks the feminine form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -a 标记阴性形式。

items.example: The suffix -ic shapes harmonic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 harmonic。

items.example: The suffix -s forms harmonicas.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成复数 harmonicas。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms harmonize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 harmonize。

items.meaning: an instrument of rubbed glass bowls
items.example: Glass harmonica keeps the learned sense.
items.exampleCN: glass harmonica 保留着学术义的痕迹。

items.meaning: mouth harmonica, an old trading name
items.meaningCN: 口琴的旧商品名，字面为「口和声」
items.example: Mundharmonika may have shaped the English use.
items.exampleCN: Mundharmonika 可能影响了英语用法。

definition_zh: 竖琴；竖琴音；弹竖琴；反复唠叨（常与 on 连用）
definition_en: a large stringed instrument played with the fingers, or to play it; also, to keep talking about something in a tiresome way
core_image: 一排长短不一的竖弦，被指尖从高到低拨过，声音像波纹一样荡开
scene: 音乐厅暗下来，演奏者双手贴住琴弦，一记和弦在大厅里缓缓散开。She eased her fingers across the harp and let the chord ring out.
sceneCN: 这里 harp 是名词，指「竖琴」（第 1 个义项：一排竖立的琴弦构成的乐器）；句意：她的手指轻轻滑过竖琴，让这个和弦久久回荡。

pos.zh: 唠叨；反复念叨（常与 on 连用）

derivatives.zh: harp（竖琴）+ -ist（表示从事某活动的人），义为「竖琴演奏者」
harp + -er（从事某动作的人），尤指旧时四处流浪弹琴的竖琴艺人
harp + -sichord（键弦复合，借自意大利语），义为「大键琴」
harp + -ing 构成动名词，义为「反复念叨；唠叨」

senses.title: A large stringed instrument
senses.definition: a large musical instrument with strings set in a frame, played by plucking them with the fingers
senses.definitionCN: 一种弦设在框架上的大型乐器，用手指拨弦发声
senses.example: A harp stood alone on the dim stage.
senses.exampleCN: 昏暗的舞台上只立着一架竖琴。
senses.why: The Latin word harpa names a hook-shaped lute, and the curved neck that gives the instrument its shape survives in the modern name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 harpa 原指钩形的琉特琴，古代乐器那个弯钩状的琴颈一直留在名字里，所以 harpa 就是「弯钩琴」。

senses.title: To play the harp
senses.definition: to perform on the harp, usually by plucking the strings with the fingertips
senses.definitionCN: 以指尖拨弦的方式演奏竖琴
senses.example: She harped softly while the guests took their seats.
senses.exampleCN: 宾客入座时，她轻轻弹着竖琴。
senses.why: Any instrument name can become a verb for the act of playing it, so the noun turns straight into an action.
senses.whyCN: 乐器名很容易直接变成「演奏它」的动词，名词 harp 一转就成了动作，指双手在琴弦上拨动的弹奏。

senses.title: To keep repeating a complaint
senses.definition: to talk or complain about the same matter again and again in a way that annoys others
senses.definitionCN: 一遍又一遍地对同一件事抱怨或念叨，令人厌烦
senses.example: He harped on the same complaint all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 整个晚上他都在念叨同一个抱怨。
senses.why: This sense is usually linked to the old phrase to harp on one string, as if a player kept striking a single note.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项一般认为与 to harp on one string 这一旧说法有关：像弹琴的人老拨同一根弦，一句话翻来覆去地弹。

senses.title: A harp-like instrument in various cultures
senses.definition: a term for many traditional stringed instruments that share the harps open string layout
senses.definitionCN: 对许多具有竖琴式开放式琴弦布局的传统乐器的统称
senses.example: The Irish harp is a national emblem.
senses.exampleCN: 爱尔兰竖琴是该国的国家象征。
senses.why: Because the medieval harp spread from Ireland to Wales and the Continent, many local frames are simply called harps.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的竖琴从爱尔兰传到威尔士与欧洲大陆，各地形状不同的琴架便都借用了 harps 这个称呼，爱尔兰竖琴更成为国家象征。

senses.title: The sound of a harp
senses.definition: the soft, rippling sound produced by plucked strings, often used to describe music that reminds one of a harp
senses.definitionCN: 拨弦发出的轻柔起伏的声音，常用来形容类似竖琴的乐声
senses.example: A harp of falling notes drifted through the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一串如竖琴般的落音在大厅里飘荡。
senses.why: The instrument name stands by synecdoche for its sound, a small step from naming the object to naming what it produces.
senses.whyCN: 用乐器名代替它发出的声音是自然的借代，于是 harp 也能从「琴」扩指「琴声」这种轻柔起伏的音响。

intro.en: Harp comes from Late Latin harpa, a hook-shaped lute, which English took through Germanic and Old English forms.
intro.cn: harp 源自晚期拉丁语 harpa（钩形琉特琴），经日耳曼语的中介进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin harpa names a stringed instrument with a curved neck.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 harpa 指名一种琴颈弯曲的弦乐器。

items.en: The word passes into Germanic forms such as Old Saxon harpa.
items.cn: 该词进入日耳曼语各支，形成古萨克森语 harpa 等形态。

items.en: Old English hearpe names the Anglo-Saxon harp, played at feasts.
items.cn: 古英语 hearpe 指盎格鲁撒克逊人的竖琴，常在宴会上弹奏。

items.en: Old French harpe and its verbal sense travel through Norman use.
items.cn: 古法语 harpe 及其动词用法随诺曼法语传开。

items.en: Harp keeps the instrument sense, adds the verb for playing, and fixes harp on as an idiom about repeating complaints.
items.cn: 现代英语保留乐器义，发展出弹奏的动词义，并把 harp on 固定成「反复抱怨」的习语。

items.en: The hook-like outline of the earliest harps is lost, but the name stays.
items.cn: 最早期竖琴的钩状轮廓早已不见，但这个名字留了下来。

note.en: Harp sits among the ancient string words and has near neighbours in harping speech about complaints.
note.cn: harp 处在古老的弦乐器词汇之间，在「抱怨」这个义场上也有邻近词。

entries.definition: a Late Latin name for a hooked stringed instrument
entries.definitionCN: 晚期拉丁语中对钩形弦乐器的称呼

entries.definition: the Old English word for a harp
entries.definitionCN: 古英语中表示竖琴的词

entries.definition: a person who plays the harp, now mainly historical
entries.definitionCN: 弹竖琴的人，如今多用于历史语境

entries.definition: an ancient U-shaped stringed instrument
entries.definitionCN: 古代的 U 形弦乐器，琴弦并排安装在两根臂之间

entries.definition: an old instrument with a rounded body and a long neck
entries.definitionCN: 古代弦乐器，琴身圆鼓、琴颈细长

entries.definition: a flat board instrument whose strings are stretched over a shallow box
entries.definitionCN: 弦平铺在浅音箱上的弦乐器

normalIntro.en: Harp is a name for a hooked stringed instrument, and the picture of one vibrating string carries over to complaints.
normalIntro.cn: harp 原是钩形弦乐器的名字，一根反复振动的琴弦的画面又延伸到了抱怨。

normal.en: Play the harp points to the instrument; a harpist is the player.
normal.cn: play the harp 指乐器本身，harpist 是演奏者。

normal.en: Harpist and harper split the roles: one is modern and trained, the other is historical and wandering.
normal.cn: harpist 与 harper 分工不同：前者是现代的专业演奏者，后者是旧时流浪的琴师。

normal.en: Harp on links the instrument to nagging, because both involve repeating one note.
normal.cn: harp on 把乐器与唠叨连在一起，因为两者都在重复同一个音。

normal.en: The Irish harp shows how far one word can reach into national symbols.
normal.cn: 爱尔兰竖琴说明一个词能延伸到何等重要的国家象征。

normal.en: Compare lyre and lute: all three are old strings, but only harp has the hollow framework.
normal.cn: 对比 lyre 与 lute：三者都是古老弦乐器，只有 harp 有中空的框架。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain of vertical strings falling in a gentle wave.
abstract.cn: 想象一排竖直的琴弦像帘幕一样轻轻起伏。

abstract.en: Imagine a fingertip touching one string over and over while others keep still.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指反复拨同一根弦，其余的弦都静止不动。

abstract.en: Think of a small metal frame worn as a badge.
abstract.cn: 想一枚小小的金属框架徽章。

examples.en: She learned to harp as a child in Dublin.
examples.cn: 她小时候在都柏林学会了弹竖琴。

examples.en: The harp in the corner was out of tune.
examples.cn: 角落里那架竖琴走音了。

examples.en: Stop harping on about the past.
examples.cn: 别总念叨过去的事了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈普」——琴弦被拨得「哈」地一声，余音又「普」地散开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 晚期拉丁语 harpa（钩形琉特琴）→ 日耳曼诸语 harpa → 古英语 hearpe → 中古英语 harpe → 现代英语 harp；核心义「一排竖弦被拨响」。harp on（反复抱怨）一般认为与 to harp on one string 的意象有关。

sensesIntro.en: Harp starts as the name of a hooked stringed instrument, becomes the act of playing it, and then stretches to the sound and, via repeating one string, to nagging.
sensesIntro.cn: harp 从钩形弦乐器的名称出发，先指弹奏这个动作，再借代指琴声，最后经由「老拨同一根弦」的意象指向唠叨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain of strings plucked in a falling wave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排琴弦被拨动，像帘幕一样层层下荡。

branches.en: The instrument sense covers both the concert harp and its traditional cousins.
branches.cn: 乐器义既包括音乐厅的竖琴，也包括各地传统竖琴类乐器。

branches.en: Playing the harp turns the object into an action.
branches.cn: 弹竖琴这个动作把名词变成了动词。

branches.en: Nagging grows from the image of striking one string again and again.
branches.cn: 唠叨义从反复拨同一根弦的画面长出来。

branches.en: Naming the object and naming its sound are two steps on the same path.
branches.cn: 称呼乐器与称呼琴声，是同一条路上的两步。

branches.en: Both the idiom and the folk frames show how far one word can be shared.
branches.cn: 习语与各地琴架都说明这个词被借用得很远。

intro.en: Harp is a borrowed instrument name built around the root harp / harp- and extended with agent and instrument suffixes.
intro.cn: harp 是借来的乐器名，围绕 harp 这一词干派生，并接上表示人和器具的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form harpa is a straight loan of an ancient instrument name, with no productive Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 harpa 是古代乐器名的直接借用，拉丁语中并没有活跃的派生家族。

definition_zh: 泼妇；悍妇；爱骂人的老妇人
definition_en: an insulting word for an old woman who is thought to be bad-tempered and always scolding
core_image: 一位老妇人拄着手杖站在门口，手指着人破口大骂，说一声就跺一下拐杖
scene: 邻居家的老太太又站在楼道里大声数落人，整层楼都听得见。The old harridan at number four shouts at every delivery boy in the street.
sceneCN: 这里 harridan 是名词，指「泼妇；爱骂人的老妇人」（第 1 个义项：刻薄好骂的老妇人）；句意：四号院那位凶巴巴的老妇人骂街上每一个送外卖的小哥。

derivatives.zh: harridan + -like（像……的），义为「泼妇似的」
同一义场的近义词：暴躁好骂的女人（非派生，仅作对照）
同义近邻：好吵闹、爱责骂的女人（非派生，仅作对照）

senses.title: A scolding old woman
senses.definition: an insulting term for an old woman who scolds and bullies the people around her
senses.definitionCN: 对刻薄好骂、动辄呵斥他人的老妇人的侮辱性称呼
senses.example: The landlady was a real harridan who shouted at everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 那个女房东真是个泼妇，见谁骂谁。
senses.why: The word was first used for a worn old horse or a broken-down hack, and the insult moved from a battered mount to a battered scolding woman.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 harridan 指一匹瘦骨嶙峋、行将报废的老马，后来这种侮辱性说法从「破旧的老坐骑」转到「刻薄好骂的老妇人」身上。

senses.title: A term of personal abuse
senses.definition: a word applied to a woman only to insult her, especially in a quarrel or in gossip
senses.definitionCN: 只在辱骂女性时使用的词，常见于争吵或闲话之中
senses.example: He called her a harridan and stalked out of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他骂她一句泼妇就甩门出去了。
senses.why: The word records how society talked about women rather than describing them, so its force is social and evaluative.
senses.whyCN: 这个词记录的是社会怎样议论女性，而不是客观描述女性，所以它的分量来自评判与指责，而不是来自外形。

senses.title: A bossy, sharp-tongued woman
senses.definition: a woman of any age described as pushy, shrill, and willing to humiliate others in public
senses.definitionCN: 对爱出风头、嗓门尖、当众羞辱别人的女人的贬称，不限年龄
senses.example: The committee chief was dismissed as a harridan in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 当地报纸把那位委员会主席贬为泼妇。
senses.why: Because scolding and bossing share the same loud public voice, the insult widened from old women to any sharp-tongued woman.
senses.whyCN: 骂人与指手画脚用的是同一种高调的公开嗓门，所以这个贬义词从老年女性扩用到了任何说话尖刻的女人。

senses.title: An obsolete sense of a worn-out horse
senses.definition: a historical sense naming a thin, broken-down horse, from which the modern insult grew
senses.definitionCN: 历史上的旧义，指瘦弱衰老的马，现代贬义即由此而来
senses.example: In old texts a harridan was the tired horse under a rider.
senses.exampleCN: 在古旧文本里，harridan 是指骑手胯下那匹疲惫的老马。
senses.why: Dictionaries of the eighteenth century still list this equine sense, showing exactly where the insult began.
senses.whyCN: 十八世纪的词典仍收录这个「马」的义项，正好说明这层侮辱是从哪里开始的。

senses.title: A stock figure in comic writing
senses.titleCN: 喜剧作品里的固定人物
senses.definition: a conventional character type in fiction and theatre, the loud older woman who controls or scolds the family
senses.definitionCN: 小说与戏剧里常见的人物类型：嗓门大、会骂人、掌控全家的年长女性
senses.example: The play gives the village harridan the funniest lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这出戏把最好笑的台词都给了村里那位泼辣的老妇人。
senses.why: Once the word meant a recognisable social figure, writers reused it as a stock type, and the insult became a dramatic role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦指认出某种社会人物，作家就把它当成固定人物来用，批评性的称呼于是变成了戏剧角色。

intro.en: Harridan appears in English in the late seventeenth century, and its origin is uncertain, with one leading suggestion pointing to a worn-out horse.
intro.cn: harridan 在十七世纪后期出现的英语里首次有记载，确切来源不确定，较有影响的一种解释指向「瘦弱的老马」。

items.en: The word is first recorded in the late 1600s with the insulting sense of a scolding woman.
items.cn: 这个词在十七世纪后期首次有记录，已是「爱骂人的女人」这层贬义。

items.en: One suggestion links it to Provencal haridelle, a thin broken-down horse.
items.cn: 一种说法认为它出自普罗旺斯语 haridelle，指瘦弱不堪的老马。

items.en: The same horse word is found in French as haridelle, meaning a gaunt old nag.
items.cn: 同源的「马」词在法语里写作 haridelle，指骨瘦如柴的老马。

items.en: Eighteenth-century dictionaries still note the horse sense alongside the insult.
items.cn: 十八世纪的词典仍同时收录「马」义与贬义。

items.en: The shift from worn horse to scolding woman is probable but not proven.
items.cn: 从老马到泼妇的语义转移只是一种较可信的推测，尚未得到证明。

items.en: Modern English keeps harridan as a strong insult and also as a comic stock type.
items.cn: 现代英语把 harridan 保留为强烈的侮辱语，同时也用作喜剧里的固定人物。

note.en: Harridan is an insult in the field of scolding women, and its shape is close to several unrelated words.
note.cn: harridan 属于「爱骂人的女人」这一义场的贬义词，拼写上也与几个不相干的词相近。

entries.definitionCN: 凶猛泼辣、带男子气的女人（正式贬称）

normalIntro.en: Harridan carries two pictures at once: an old nag and a voice that will not stop.
normalIntro.cn: harridan 同时装着一匹马和一把停不下来的嗓子：老马加骂声。

normal.en: The likely source haridelle is French for a scraggy old horse.
normal.cn: 可能的来源词 haridelle 在法语里指瘦弱的老马。

normal.en: Old texts list the horse sense, so the insult began as a comparison.
normal.cn: 古旧文本里收录过「马」这个义项，可见这一贬义起初是一种比喻。

normal.en: An old harridan is the standard collocation for a scolding old woman.
normal.cn: an old harridan 是说爱骂人的老妇人的固定搭配。

normal.en: Compare shrew and termagant: same field, but harridan is more dated and harsher.
normal.cn: 对比 shrew 与 termagant：属于同一义场，harridan 更显过时也更重。

normal.en: Use it carefully: it is an insult aimed at people, not a neutral description.
normal.cn: 用时要小心：它是针对人的侮辱语，不是中性描述。

abstract.en: Picture a thin old horse refusing to move while its rider shouts.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹瘦弱的老马赖着不走，骑手在一旁大喊。

abstract.en: Imagine a wooden door banged open before every sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象每说一句话，木门就被人摔开一次。

abstract.en: Think of a face that is all frown and open mouth.
abstract.cn: 想一张只剩下皱着眉和张开嘴的脸。

examples.en: The gossip column described the manager as a harridan.
examples.cn: 八卦专栏把那位女经理写成了泼妇。

examples.en: Two harridans argued over the washing line for an hour.
examples.cn: 两个爱骂人的老妇人为一根晾衣绳吵了一小时。

examples.en: Calling a colleague a harridan in a meeting is deeply sexist.
examples.cn: 在会上把同事骂成泼妇，是非常有性别偏见的行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈里蛋」——姓哈里的老太太天天骂人，人人都躲她，连鸡蛋都她说了算；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为来自普罗旺斯语 haridelle（瘦弱的老马），同形词见于法语；该词在十七世纪后期进入英语时已带「爱骂人的女人」的贬义，由「破旧的老坐骑」转为对刻薄老妇人的侮辱性称呼。另一种解释把它当作十九世纪的人物绰号，证据不足。

sensesIntro.en: Harridan names a worn-out horse, then a scolding woman, then any sharp-tongued woman, and finally a stock character in comedy.
sensesIntro.cn: harridan 先指瘦弱的老马，再指爱骂人的老妇人，然后扩指任何嘴尖的女人，最后成为喜剧里的固定角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rail-thin old nag with a voice that never stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹瘦骨嶙峋的老马，配上一把停不下来的骂人嗓子。

branches.en: The standard modern insult is the scolding old woman.
branches.cn: 现代最主要的贬义是刻薄好骂的老妇人。

branches.en: Its use in abuse shows that the word is evaluative, not descriptive.
branches.cn: 它被用于辱骂，说明这个词带评判而非描述。

branches.en: The sharp-tongued woman sense drops the age limit.
branches.cn: 「嘴尖的女人」这层义项去掉了年龄限制。

branches.en: The historical horse sense is the visible seed of the insult.
branches.cn: 历史上的「老马」义是这层贬义看得见的种子。

branches.en: The same figure moves from neighbours to stage characters.
branches.cn: 同一个形象从街坊邻居搬到了舞台角色上。

intro.en: Harridan has no living English suffix of its own; English builds almost nothing on it beyond -like.
intro.cn: harridan 本身没有活跃的英语后缀，英语在它之上几乎只派生出 -like 的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin offers no related family, so the loan looks to Occitan and French romance words instead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有同族词，这个词的来源要到普罗旺斯语与法语的材料里去找。

derivatives.zh: 泼妇似的

definition_zh: 麻烦；烦扰；争论；争执；不断烦扰；纠缠
definition_en: a lot of annoying trouble or a noisy argument, or to keep annoying someone with repeated demands
core_image: 行李袋的拉链卡住又断掉，箱子散了一地，人只能蹲在地上一件件往回塞
scene: 签证材料又要补交一份，还得排队重排号，她忍不住抱怨这趟出门太折腾。Getting a visa turned into a hassle she had not expected.
sceneCN: 这里 hassle 是名词，指「麻烦；烦扰」（第 1 个义项：令人烦恼费事的麻烦）；句意：办签证成了一件她没料到的麻烦事。

collocations.phrase: go to the hassle of doing something

derivatives.zh: hassle（麻烦）+ -free（没有……的），义为「省心的；无麻烦的」
hassle 加 -ed 作分词形容词，义为「被弄得心烦的；被纠缠的」
hassle + -ing 构成动名词，义为「反复骚扰；纠缠」

senses.title: Annoying trouble
senses.definition: a situation or task that is irritating and takes unwanted effort and time
senses.definitionCN: 令人恼火、需要额外花时间和力气的情况或事情
senses.example: Filling in the forms was a hassle.
senses.exampleCN: 填那些表格真是一件麻烦事。
senses.why: The American dialect word started as a noisy quarrel, and a quarrel that drags on became the picture of any annoying effort.
senses.whyCN: 这个美式方言词最初指一场吵闹的争吵，而一场拖不完的口角就成了「任何费心费力之事」的画面。

senses.title: To bother someone repeatedly
senses.definition: to keep troubling or pressuring someone, often with repeated requests or demands
senses.definitionCN: 不断地麻烦或施压于某人，常表现为反复的要求或催问
senses.example: Journalists hassled her outside the court.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们在法院外纠缠她。
senses.why: From a noisy dispute as a thing, the word turned into the action of pestering someone until they agree.
senses.whyCN: 当争吵从「事情」转为「动作」，就变成了不停纠缠某人的行为，直到对方妥协为止。

senses.title: A noisy argument
senses.definition: an angry quarrel, especially one involving shouting and confusion
senses.definitionCN: 激烈的口角，尤指夹杂喊叫与混乱的争吵
senses.example: There was a hassle over who had paid for the tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 为了谁买了票，双方吵了一场。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, and it still survives in British dialect as a heated dispute.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的义项，至今仍在英国方言中表示一场热吵的争论，和「麻烦」义其实是同一场景的两面。

senses.title: Trouble on the road or airport
senses.definition: the delays, queues, and queueing trouble that make a journey or a service irksome
senses.definitionCN: 让旅程或服务变得折腾的延误、排队与来回奔波
senses.example: The hassle of changing planes put her off flying.
senses.exampleCN: 转机的折腾让她不想再坐飞机。
senses.why: Because travel is the setting where the original American sense of trouble crystallised, the word keeps this concrete scene.
senses.whyCN: 出行正是这个美式「麻烦」义定型的具体场景，所以 hassle 在交通与服务的语境里格外常用。

senses.title: To harass a worker or customer
senses.definition: to press someone at work with constant calls, messages, or demands, often considered harassment
senses.definitionCN: 用不断的电话、信息或要求施压于在职人员或客户，常被视为骚扰
senses.example: She complained that her former employer hassled her every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她抱怨前雇主每周都来纠缠她。
senses.why: The pestering sense grows concrete at work, where repeated messages turn a minor nuisance into a grievance.
senses.whyCN: 纠缠义在工作场所变得具体：反复的信息让小小的烦扰升级成可以投诉的委屈，甚至构成骚扰。

intro.en: Hassle is an American dialect word of uncertain origin, usually explained as a variant of haggle and first recorded in the late nineteenth century.
intro.cn: hassle 是来源不确定的美式方言词，一般认为与 haggle（讨价还价）有关，十九世纪末开始在英语里出现。

items.en: Hassle appears in American speech at first as a heated dispute or tussle.
items.cn: harass 并非它的来源，hassle 在十九世纪后期的美国口语里首先指一场激烈的争论或扭打。

items.en: The first recorded use turns on noisy quarrelling in a crowd.
items.cn: 最早的记录用法讲的是人群中的吵闹争执。

items.en: Most dictionaries relate it to haggle, which covers both arguing and bargaining, though haggle itself is also of uncertain etymology.
items.cn: 多数词典认为它与 haggle（既指争论也指讨价还价）有关，但 haggle 本身的来源也不确定。

items.en: Some link the hagg element to Norse haggva, to cut, but this remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 有人把其中 hag 这一部分追溯到古诺尔斯语 haggva（砍），这只是重构形式，未获确证。

items.en: The noun broadens from quarrel to any annoying trouble, and a verb for pestering someone develops.
items.cn: 名词从「争吵」扩展到「一切烦人的麻烦」，由它又发展出「纠缠某人」的动词。

items.en: British usage adopts the American fuss sense and favours the phrase without the hassle.
items.cn: 英式用法接受了美式的「麻烦」义，并常用 without the hassle 这一说法。

note.en: Hassle mixes quarrel and nuisance, so its neighbours include both trouble words and pestering words.
note.cn: hassle 同时掺着「争吵」与「麻烦」，所以它的近邻既有表示麻烦的词，也有表示纠缠的词。

entries.definition: to hurry or push people along
entries.definitionCN: 催促；推搡；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to move fast with great force
entries.definitionCN: 猛冲；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: made weary by repeated pressure
entries.definitionCN: 被反复施压弄得心力交瘁的

entries.definition: a person or thing that annoys
entries.definitionCN: 令人讨厌的人或事

entries.definition: to keep annoying someone with requests
entries.definitionCN: 以要求不断烦扰某人

entries.definition: to keep complaining at someone until they give in
entries.definitionCN: 唠叨不停，直到对方让步

normalIntro.en: Hassle is a quarrel that turns into a chore: the same noisy push becomes the trouble you must deal with.
normalIntro.cn: hassle 是一场变成苦差的争吵：同一股吵闹的折腾，最后成了必须处理的麻烦。

normal.en: It is most often linked to haggle, the word for arguing over a price.
normal.cn: 它最常被认为与 haggle（为价钱争执）同源。

normal.en: A real hassle is the standard phrase for tiresome effort.
normal.cn: a real hassle 是说某件事很费劲的固定说法。

normal.en: The verb takes about or for: hassle someone about money.
normal.cn: 动词常接 about 或 for，指为某事纠缠某人。

normal.en: Without the hassle shows how British speakers use it.
normal.cn: without the hassle 体现英式用法中对「麻烦」义的偏爱。

normal.en: Compare nuisance for a thing that annoys and pester for the action of annoying.
normal.cn: 对比 nuisance（烦人的事物）与 pester（烦扰的动作）。

abstract.en: Picture a zipper that jams just as you need to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象你正要出门时拉链卡死的那一下。

abstract.en: Imagine a queue that moves one person every ten minutes.
abstract.cn: 想象一列十分钟才挪一个人的队。

abstract.en: Think of a phone that keeps buzzing with reminders.
abstract.cn: 想一部被提醒消息震个不停的手机。

examples.en: Ordering online saves you the hassle of parking downtown.
examples.cn: 网上订购能省去在市中心停车的麻烦。

examples.en: Stop hassling me about the rent.
examples.cn: 别再为房租的事烦我了。

examples.en: The transfer was simple and completely hassle-free.
examples.cn: 转账过程简单，完全不用操心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈撕」——两个人对着哈气、撕来撕去，越吵越麻烦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为与方言词 haggle（讨价还价、争执）同源或为其变体，十九世纪末在美国口语中首次记录，最初指争吵、扭打这类吵闹的争执，再由「争吵」引申为「费事的麻烦」，并发展出「纠缠」的动词义。

sensesIntro.en: Hassle begins as a noisy quarrel, turns into the trouble that quarrel causes, then into the act of pestering and the delays that pester travellers and workers.
sensesIntro.cn: hassle 从一场吵闹的争吵开始，转为争吵带来的麻烦，再引申为纠缠他人的动作，以及纠缠出行者和上班族的种种折腾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jammed zipper that turns a short trip into a long struggle.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡死的拉链把一小段路变成一场苦战。

branches.en: The main modern sense is trouble that costs unwanted effort.
branches.cn: 现代主流的义项是让人白费力气的麻烦。

branches.en: The verb and its workplace use name the pressure put on people.
branches.cn: 动词义与它在职场的用法，说的都是加在人身上的压力。

branches.en: The quarrel sense is the oldest layer and still lives in dialect.
branches.cn: 争吵义是最早的层次，至今仍活在方言里。

branches.en: Travel is where the trouble sense is most vivid.
branches.cn: 出行是「麻烦」义最鲜活的场景。

branches.en: A delayed journey and a stuck zipper are the same word-faced nuisance.
branches.cn: 误点的旅程和卡死的拉链属于同一种迎面而来的烦扰。

intro.en: Hassle is a dialect word with almost no inherited affixes, so English adds only -free, -ed, and -ing to it.
intro.cn: hassle 是方言来源的词，几乎没有继承下来的构词成分，英语只是在它上面加 -free、-ed、-ing。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family behind the word, so only later Latin-derived words adjoining the field are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁语词族，仅列出义场上相关的后起拉丁词。

items.example: Haggle is the likely relative of hassle.
items.exampleCN: haggle 是 hassle 可能的亲缘词。

items.example: Hassle keeps the noun senses.
items.exampleCN: hassle 保留这些名词义项。

items.example: The verb is built on the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词义由名词义发展而来。

items.example: The suffix -free forms hassle-free.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -free 构成 hassle-free。

items.example: Hassle-free is common in advertising.
items.exampleCN: hassle-free 常见于广告语。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms hassled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 hassled。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms hassling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 hassling。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms nuisances in the same field.
items.exampleCN: 同一义场里的 nuisance 也带这类似后缀。

definition_zh: 加速；促使；赶快；急忙做
definition_en: to make something happen sooner or more quickly, or to act quickly yourself
core_image: 赶车人挥起鞭子，车轮转得越来越快
scene: 病人一见情况不妙就打电话叫医生，好让诊断来得早点。Worried by the fever, she hastened to call the doctor.
sceneCN: 这里 hasten 是「赶快做；急忙做」（第 3 个义项：自己迅速行动）；句意：她被高烧吓到，急忙打电话叫医生。

derivatives.zh: 急忙；仓促；词根名词，hasten 的直接来源
匆忙的；草率的；由 haste 加 -y 构成
匆忙地；草率地；由 hasty 加 -ly 构成

senses.title: To make something happen sooner
senses.definition: to cause an event to happen sooner, or more quickly than it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使某件事比原本更早或更快地发生
senses.example: The new motorway hastened the growth of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 新建的高速公路加快了城镇的发展。
senses.why: The core image of hurrying is turned outward: one thing acts as the whip that pushes an event onward.
senses.whyCN: 「急着赶路」的核心意象向外投射：某物充当鞭子，把事件往前推。

senses.title: To make a bad outcome come sooner
senses.definition: to make the end of something, especially something harmful, arrive earlier
senses.definitionCN: 使某种结局，尤指有害的结局，更早到来
senses.example: Heavy debts hastened the collapse of the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 沉重的债务加速了这家公司的倒闭。
senses.why: The same push can be aimed at decline or death, so the verb also names what speeds up an unhappy end.
senses.whyCN: 同一种推动也可指向衰落或死亡，于是这个词也用来指让不幸结局提早到来。

senses.title: To go or act quickly yourself
senses.definition: to move or do something with speed, especially to avoid delay or danger
senses.definitionCN: 迅速移动或做事，尤指为了避开延误或危险
senses.example: She hastened back to the office to fetch the key.
senses.exampleCN: 她急忙赶回办公室去取钥匙。
senses.why: Here the subject is the one who is whipped: the verb describes a person hurrying, usually with a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这里主语是被催赶的人：动词描述一个人匆匆行动，通常带有目的。

senses.title: To say something immediately to soften it
senses.titleCN: 赶紧补一句（以缓和语气）
senses.definition: to add a remark at once so that a strong statement will not sound too harsh
senses.definitionCN: 立刻补上一句话，以免先前的强烈说法听起来过于苛刻
senses.example: The minister denied the rumour, hastening to add that an inquiry would follow.
senses.exampleCN: 部长否认了传言，随即补充说将会展开调查。
senses.why: The push to act quickly is applied to speech, and a quick addition can smooth what has just been said.
senses.whyCN: 把「赶快行动」用在说话上，迅速补充的内容可以缓和刚说出口的话。

senses.title: To move a process forward in order to finish it
senses.definition: to speed up an official or practical process so that it reaches its end sooner
senses.definitionCN: 加快官方或实际事务的办理，使其更早结束
senses.example: The court hastened the trial after new evidence appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据出现后，法院加快了审判进程。
senses.why: When the thing being pushed is a routine procedure, hurrying turns into a practical and neutral sense of speeding it up.
senses.whyCN: 被推动的对象若是例行程序，催促就变成一种中性、实务性的加快办理。

senses.title: To grow faster than nature allows
senses.definition: to develop a plant or creature too fast, often in a way that harms it
senses.definitionCN: 使植物或生物过快生长，往往反而对其有害
senses.example: Growers hasten the ripening of the fruit under lamps.
senses.exampleCN: 种植者用灯照让水果提早成熟。
senses.why: In farming, forcing growth forward leads to the modern sense of bringing plants or creatures on too quickly.
senses.whyCN: 在农业中把生长往前赶，引出「把植物或生物催得过快」的现代义项。

intro.en: Hasten is built in English from the French noun haste, so its story begins with an idea of hurry rather than a separate root.
intro.cn: hasten 是英语借法语名词 haste 自行构成的派生动词，故事从「匆忙」这个概念讲起，而不是另有一个独立词根。

items.en: A Germanic word for a state of violent hurry, often written haist, is thought to be the source of the family.
items.cn: 一般认为该词族源自一个日耳曼词语，表示猛烈的匆忙状态，常写作 haist。

items.en: Haste and the verb haster pass into French, where haster already means to hurry and to drive on.
items.cn: haste 与动词 haster 进入法语，haster 已兼有「赶紧」与「催促」两义。

items.en: English borrows haste and the verb hasten from French, first in the sense of hurrying.
items.cn: 英语约在中古英语时期从法语借入 haste 与动词 hasten，最初表示匆忙赶路。

items.en: Dictionaries date the modern transitive sense, to shorten the time of something, from around 1560.
items.cn: 词典把现代及物用法，即缩短某事所需时间，定在约十六世纪中叶。

items.en: In the eighteenth century British spelling settled the silent group -en-, while American spelling also planned it.
items.cn: 十八世纪英国拼写法固定了不发音的 -en- 组合，美国拼写也随之定型。

items.en: Today hasten is mostly formal or literary, while its relatives haste and hasty stay everyday words.
items.cn: 今天 hasten 多为正式或书面用法，而同族的 haste 与 hasty 仍是日常词。

note.en: Group one holds the haste family and its look-alikes; group two holds verbs of speeding something up.
note.cn: 第一组是 haste 词族及形近词；第二组是表示加速、催促的动词。

entries.definition: great speed in doing something, often too little care
entries.definitionCN: 做事的急速，常指过于仓促

entries.definition: done or made too quickly to be careful
entries.definitionCN: 匆忙的；草率的

entries.definition: The verb built on haste by adding -en, the same way fresh becomes freshen.
entries.definitionCN: 由 haste 加词尾 -en 构成的动词，与 fresh 变 freshen 的方式相同。

entries.definition: to move or make something move quickly, used in speech far more often than hasten
entries.definitionCN: 赶快或使赶快，口语频率远高于 hasten

entries.definition: to make a process go faster, common in science and economics
entries.definitionCN: 使过程加快，常用于科学与经济领域

entries.definition: to make an official task or order be dealt with sooner
entries.definitionCN: 加速办理公务或订单

normalIntro.en: Hasten is haste plus -en, the ending that turns a state into an action.
normalIntro.cn: hasten 就是 haste 加 -en，这个词尾把状态变成动作。

normal.en: The -en ending turns the noun haste into a verb, as fresh becomes freshen.
normal.cn: 词尾 -en 把名词 haste 变成动词，就像 fresh 变 freshen。

normal.en: Hasten back, hasten to add, and hasten the process cover most exam uses.
normal.cn: 「急忙赶回」「赶紧补充」「加快进程」覆盖了考试中最常见的用法。

normal.en: Remember hasty, its adjective, with the meaning careless because of speed.
normal.cn: 记住同族形容词 hasty，意为因求快而不够细心。

normal.en: Two different things are both called hasty: a quick movement and a careless decision.
normal.cn: 同一个 hasty 可修饰两种对象：快速的行动与草率的决定。

normal.en: In formal writing, use hasten for what makes an event come sooner.
normal.cn: 正式写作中，用 hasten 表示让事件提早发生。

abstract.en: Picture a driver cracking a whip, and the cart lurching forward.
abstract.cn: 想象车夫甩响鞭子，板车猛地向前一冲。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands are spinning much too fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟表的指针转得快得不正常。

abstract.en: See a person running for the last bus while tying a scarf.
abstract.cn: 眼前浮现一个人一边系围巾一边奔向末班车。

examples.en: Poor harvests hastened the fall of the ancient city.
examples.cn: 歉收加速了这座古城的衰亡。

examples.en: She hastened to add that the figures were only provisional.
examples.cn: 她赶紧补充说这些数字只是暂定的。

examples.en: The firm hastened the delivery by hiring extra staff.
examples.cn: 公司增聘人手，加快了交货速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑死人」——想到瘟疫会「加速」人的死亡，于是记住 hasten 表加速；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语中表示急躁的词形，经法语 haster（催促）与名词 haste（匆忙）进入英语；英语在 haste 上加 -en 构成 hasten，核心义「催着自己或别人往前赶」。

sensesIntro.en: Hasten starts with making an event come sooner, turns the same push toward bad endings, then describes the hurrying subject, quick remarks, hurried processes, and forced growth.
sensesIntro.cn: hasten 先指使事件提早发生，再把同一种推动转向坏结局，随后描述匆忙的主语、赶紧补话、加快办理与催生过早成熟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whip cracked so that the wheels turn faster.
core.cn: 核心意象：鞭子一响，车轮转得更快。

branches.en: Making an event come sooner is the outward push on things.
branches.cn: 使事件提早发生，是把推动力施加在事物上。

branches.en: When the event is harmful, the push hastens decline or ruin.
branches.cn: 若事件本身有害，这种推动就是加速衰落或毁灭。

branches.en: The person who hurries is the receiver of that push.
branches.cn: 匆忙的人就是被推动的一方。

branches.en: Speed applied to talk or paperwork yields the softening remark and the hurried process.
branches.cn: 把速度用于言语或公务，就得到缓和的补充与加快办理。

branches.en: A forced end and forced growth share the idea of too much speed.
branches.cn: 被迫到来的结局与催生过早成熟，共有的都是速度过快。

intro.en: Hasten grows by the verb ending -en, and the haste family spreads through adjectival -y and adverbial -ly.
intro.cn: hasten 靠动词词尾 -en 构成，haste 词族再通过 -y 与 -ly 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies no direct source for haste, but festinare, properare, and ruina show the same ideas of hurrying and rushing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语并非 haste 的直接来源，但 festinare、properare、ruina 体现着相同的「赶快」与「冲撞」意象。

items.meaning: to make something so, or to put it into a state
items.meaningCN: 使变得；使进入某种状态
items.example: The suffix turns haste into hasten.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把 haste 变成 hasten。

items.meaning: hurry, often with too little care
items.example: Haste supplies the core meaning, as in the verb hasten, the adjective hasty, and the adverb hastily.
items.exampleCN: haste 提供核心含义，体现为动词 hasten、形容词 hasty 与副词 hastily。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix turns haste into hasty, which then yields hastily and the verb hasten.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把 haste 变成 hasty，再派生出 hastily 与动词 hasten。

items.example: The suffix forms hastily from hasty.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾由 hasty 构成 hastily。

items.example: Hastening appears as a participle.
items.exampleCN: hastening 可作分词使用。

items.meaning: done too quickly to be careful
items.example: A hasty decision is often regretted.
items.exampleCN: 草率的决定常令人后悔。

items.example: Over- adds the idea of too much.
items.exampleCN: over- 加了「过度」的意思。

items.example: The French noun is the English source.
items.exampleCN: 法语名词是英语的来源。

items.example: He left hastily at noon.
items.exampleCN: 他中午匆匆离开。

definition_zh: 匆忙的；草率的；仓促的；轻率的
definition_en: done or made too quickly to be careful, or moving with too much speed
core_image: 还没看清路就踩下油门，结果冲进了沟里
scene: 面试前一天晚上，他才匆忙改了一版简历，连错字都没检查。A hasty revision of the resume left several errors.
sceneCN: 这里 hasty 是「匆忙做出的；草率的」（第 2 个义项：因求快而欠缺细致）；句意：匆忙修改简历，留下了好几处错误。

derivatives.zh: 匆忙地；草率地；由 hasty 加 -ly 构成
匆忙；草率；由 hasty 加 -ness 构成
加速；赶快；由 haste 加 -en 构成的同族动词

senses.title: Moving or done with great speed
senses.definition: done, made, or moving quickly, with little time to spare
senses.definitionCN: 很快完成、做出或移动，几乎没有余裕
senses.example: They made a hasty departure before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在暴风雨来临前匆忙离开了。
senses.why: The adjective comes straight from the noun haste, so speed itself is the first thing it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接来自名词 haste，所以它首先描述的就是「快」。

senses.title: Too quick to be careful
senses.definition: done so quickly that mistakes are made and care is missing
senses.definitionCN: 做得太快以至于出错，缺少细致的考虑
senses.example: Do not draw hasty conclusions from one small study.
senses.exampleCN: 不要只凭一份小研究就草率地下结论。
senses.why: Because haste leaves no time to check, the word easily shifts from a speed to a criticism of that speed.
senses.whyCN: 由于匆忙没有时间检查，这个词便从「快」滑向「快得不对」的批评。

senses.title: Quick to anger or to act emotionally
senses.definition: acting or reacting too fast, especially in the way a person speaks or treats others
senses.definitionCN: 行动或反应过快，尤指人说话或待人时不够稳妥
senses.example: Avoid being hasty with people who have just been told bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 对刚得知坏消息的人，不要急躁行事。
senses.why: A hasty mind jumps before it thinks, so the criticism is applied to people as well as to actions.
senses.whyCN: 急躁的人还没想清楚就已行动，因此这个批评也用于形容人而不只是行为。

senses.title: Brief and hurried, in food or rest
senses.definition: short and done in a hurry, as with a meal, a nap, or a wash
senses.definitionCN: 时间很短且做得匆忙，如吃饭、小睡或洗漱
senses.example: We had a hasty lunch in the café downstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在楼下咖啡店匆匆吃了午饭。
senses.why: Everyday objects such as meals and washes take on the adjective when they are squeezed into a spare minute.
senses.whyCN: 吃饭、洗漱这类日常之事被挤进几分钟里时，就自然地配上这个形容词。

intro.en: Hasty is the adjective made from the noun haste, so it shares the French and Germanic prehistory of the haste family.
intro.cn: hasty 是由名词 haste 加词尾构成的形容词，与 haste 词族共享法语与日耳曼语的更早来源。

items.en: A Germanic word for violent hurry, often written haifst or haist, is thought to lie behind the family.
items.cn: 一般认为该词族的背后是一个日耳曼词语，表示猛烈的匆忙，常写作 haifst 或 haist。

items.en: The French noun haste and the adjective hastif enter the record in the twelfth century.
items.cn: 法语名词 haste 与形容词 hastif 在十二世纪见于记载。

items.en: English borrows the adjective as hastif, which is later reshaped into hasty.
items.cn: 英语先借入形容词 hastif，后来改形为 hasty。

items.en: Hasty settles into the senses of quick, sudden, and heedless that we still use.
items.cn: hasty 稳定为「快速、突然、不顾后果」等今天仍在使用的义项。

items.en: The adjective keeps formal and journalistic uses, often in phrases such as a hasty retreat.
items.cn: 该形容词在现代英语中多用于正式或报刊文体，常见于「仓促撤退」一类短语。

note.en: Group one collects the haste word family and near-spellings; group two collects adjectives of speed.
note.cn: 第一组是 haste 词族与拼写相近的词；第二组是表示速度与急切的形容词。

entries.definition: the noun that hasty was built from, meaning excessive speed
entries.definitionCN: hasty 由之构成的名词，意为过快的速度

entries.definition: the adverb formed by adding -ly, meaning in a hasty way
entries.definitionCN: 加 -ly 构成的副词，意为匆忙地

entries.definition: the related verb meaning to hurry or to speed something up
entries.definitionCN: 同族动词，意为赶快或加速

entries.definition: fast, described without any suggestion of criticism
entries.definitionCN: 快的，不带批评意味

entries.definition: acting too quickly with no thought at all, a stronger criticism than hasty
entries.definitionCN: 毫无考虑就行动，贬义比 hasty 更强

entries.definition: sudden and often unwelcome, describing the shock that the speed causes
entries.definitionCN: 突然且常令人不适，强调速度造成的冲击

entries.definition: done at once because of a feeling, without any planning
entries.definitionCN: 凭一时的感觉立刻行动，毫无计划

normalIntro.en: Hasty is haste plus the adjective -y, and both words carry the feeling of speed that has gone past careful.
