normalIntro.cn: hasty 就是 haste 加形容词词尾 -y，两个词都带着「快过了头、顾不上细致」的感觉。

normal.en: The -y ending turns haste into an adjective, as in rain becoming rainy.
normal.cn: 词尾 -y 把 haste 变成形容词，就像 rain 变 rainy。

normal.en: Adverbs from hasty are hastier when they happen quickly, as in coming sooner.
normal.cn: 做动作的方式由副词 hastily 承担，形容词 hasty 只修饰名词。

normal.en: A hasty retreat is the most fixed phrase in newspapers.
normal.cn: 「匆忙撤退」是报刊中最固定的搭配。

normal.en: The three common partners are a hasty decision, a hasty conclusion, and a hasty breakfast.
normal.cn: 三个最常见的搭配是「草率的决定」「仓促的结论」与「匆匆的早餐」。

normal.en: Compare hasty with the verb hasten, which pushes an event forward.
normal.cn: 把 hasty 与动词 hasten 对比：后者把事件往前推。

abstract.en: Picture a hand grabbing papers off a desk so fast that they scatter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手飞快抓起桌上的纸张，纸却被带得四处飞散。

abstract.en: Imagine a driver who joins the road without checking the mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象一位司机没看后视镜就并道。

abstract.en: See someone eating a sandwich while already standing at the door.
abstract.cn: 眼前浮现一个人还没出门就先站着吃完三明治。

examples.en: The manager apologised for the hasty reply.
examples.cn: 经理为仓促的回复道歉。

examples.en: They beat a hasty retreat when the rain began.
examples.cn: 雨一下起来，他们就匆忙撤退了。

examples.en: A hasty decision at this stage could cost the team the season.
examples.cn: 在现阶段做出草率的决定，可能让球队输掉整个赛季。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑死」——听到「黑死」就夺路而逃，动作只能是 hasty；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自古法语名词 haste（匆忙），更早可回溯到日耳曼语的 haist；英语借入形容词 hastif 后改写为 hasty，核心义「快得不留余地」。

sensesIntro.en: Hasty first just means quick, then criticises that quickness as careless, then moves on to hot tempers and to brief, squeezed-in pieces of daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: hasty 先只表示「快」，再对这份快提出「不细致」的批评，进而形容急躁的脾性，以及被挤进零碎时间的日常片段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot pressing the accelerator before checking the road ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没看清水前就一脚踩下油门。

branches.en: Speed alone is the plain descriptive sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的速度，是最平实的描述性义项。

branches.en: The same speed becomes a fault when care is lost.
branches.cn: 同样的速度在失去细致后就成了缺点。

branches.en: The fault is then seen in people and in their reactions.
branches.cn: 这一缺点随后表现在人及其反应上。

branches.en: Meals and naps squeezed into spare minutes wear the same label.
branches.cn: 挤进零碎时间的吃饭与小睡也带着同样的标签。

branches.en: Both the careless action and the hasty temper blame speed for a poor result.
branches.cn: 草率的行为与急躁的脾气，都把坏结果归因于过快。

intro.en: Hasty is a borrowed adjective shaped by the native -y ending, and the haste family spreads through -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: hasty 是借来的形容词，配上了英语的 -y 词尾，haste 词族再经 -ly 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives no direct origin, but praeceps, temerarius, and subitus express the same falling-forward and unchecked rushing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语并非直接来源，但 praeceps、temerarius、subitus 表达了相同的「前扑」与「不加制止」意象。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix builds hasty from haste, as in rainy from rain.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾由 haste 构成 hasty，与 rainy 来自 rain 相同。

items.example: Haste supplies the core meaning of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: haste 提供该形容词的核心含义。

items.example: The borrowed form was later reshaped into hasty.
items.exampleCN: 借入的旧形后来被改写成 hasty。

items.example: The suffix forms hastily from hasty.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾由 hasty 构成 hastily。

items.example: The suffix forms hastiness from hasty.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾由 hasty 构成 hastiness。

items.example: The suffix forms hastier.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成比较级 hastier。

items.example: The suffix forms hastiest.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成最高级 hastiest。

items.example: Hastiness is a fault in busy work.
items.exampleCN: 在忙碌的工作中，草率是一种缺点。

items.example: Over- marks the extreme of haste.
items.exampleCN: over- 标出「匆忙」的极端。

definition_zh: 孵化；孵出；（蛋）破壳；策划；密谋；舱口；后备厢盖
definition_en: to break out of an egg or cause an egg to open, to plan something secretly, or a small covered opening
core_image: 蛋壳上先是裂开一道细缝，接着一只湿漉漉的小鸟把头探出来
scene: 一枚枚蛋排在暖灯下，小鸟一只只从壳里钻出来。A dozen eggs waited under the lamp to hatch.
sceneCN: 这里 hatch 是「孵化；（蛋）破壳」（第 2 个义项：幼体破壳钻出）；句意：十来枚蛋在灯下等待着孵化。

derivatives.zh: 孵化场；由 hatch 加 -ery 构成
孵化；也指美术中的交叉排线
刚孵出的幼体；hatch 加 -ling 构成

senses.title: To open an egg by breaking it
senses.definition: to sit on eggs, keeping them warm until the young birds break out of them
senses.definitionCN: 伏在蛋上保持其温暖，直到幼鸟破壳而出
senses.example: The hen hatched five eggs that spring.
senses.exampleCN: 那年春天，母鸡孵出了五只小鸡。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense comes from the Old English word for the action of a bird breaking its way out.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的实体义项来自古英语中描述鸟「破壳钻出」动作的词。

senses.title: To come out of an egg
senses.definition: for a young creature to break its shell and emerge
senses.definitionCN: 幼体破开蛋壳并钻出来
senses.example: The chicks hatched after three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 小鸡在三周后孵了出来。
senses.why: The same verb takes the egg or the chick as its subject, so shell-breaking can be seen from either side.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也可以让蛋或小鸡作主语，破壳的动作可从两侧来看。

senses.title: To plan something in secret
senses.definition: to develop a plan quietly, often something dishonest or surprising
senses.definitionCN: 暗中酝酿计划，常指不正当或出人意料的计划
senses.example: Two directors were hatching a takeover bid.
senses.exampleCN: 两位董事正在暗中策划收购方案。
senses.why: A plan hidden at first and suddenly revealed looks much like a chick hidden inside a shell until it breaks out.
senses.whyCN: 计划先藏后露，就像蛋壳里的小鸟直到破壳才现身，这个画面自然引向「密谋」。

senses.title: A small covered opening in a surface
senses.definition: a small door or opening in a floor, deck, or wall, often covered by a lid
senses.definitionCN: 地板、甲板或墙上带盖的小门或开口
senses.example: The engineer climbed down through the hatch to the engine room.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师从舱口下到机房。
senses.why: A separate Old English noun for a door paved the way for the nautical sense of an opening in a deck.
senses.whyCN: 古英语另有一个表示「门」的名词，为后来航海中的「甲板开口」义项铺了路。

senses.title: A back door in a vehicle
senses.definition: the rear door or lid of a hatchback car that opens upward
senses.definitionCN: 掀背式汽车向上开启的后门或后盖
senses.example: She lifted the hatch and slid the bags inside.
senses.exampleCN: 她掀起后备厢盖，把包塞了进去。
senses.why: The opening sense is grafted onto the car body, naming the lid that lifts like the old deck hatches.
senses.whyCN: 「开口」义被移植到车身上，用来指像旧日甲板舱口那样向上掀起的盖子。

senses.title: To be the process that decides an outcome
senses.definition: to be the setting in which an idea or an event is quietly produced and then appears
senses.definitionCN: 成为某种想法或事件悄悄产生、最终现身的场所
senses.example: The small workshop hatched most of the designs the company later sold.
senses.exampleCN: 公司后来卖出的多数设计，都是在那间小作坊里酝酿出来的。
senses.why: From the hidden plan, the verb spreads to any place where new things are quietly produced before they emerge.
senses.whyCN: 从秘密计划进一步泛化，这个词也指新事物现身前悄悄产生的任何场所。

intro.en: English has three words spelled hatch: the bird verb comes from a native verb, the opening noun from a native word for a door, and the crossing-of-lines noun is a later borrowing. Only the first two belong to this entry.
intro.cn: 英语中拼作 hatch 的同形词有三类：表示鸟的词来自本族动词，表示开口的名词来自本族「门」词，表示交叉排线的名词则是后来的借词；本条目只收前两类。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as hakan is thought to underlie the Old English words for hatching.
items.cn: 一般认为古英语「孵化」诸词背后有一个类似 hakan 的重构形式。

items.en: Hæccan means to hatch, and hæc or hæcc names a hatch, from a word for a door or gate.
items.cn: hæccan 意为孵化，hæc 或 hæcc 指舱口、小门，词义源自表示「门」的词。

items.en: Hatch loses the old k sound and settles on the modern spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，hatch 失去旧有的 k 音，拼写与读音固定下来。

items.en: Ship decks and their openings are called hatches, spreading the opening sense to engineering.
items.cn: 早期现代英语中，船的甲板开口被称为 hatch，并把「开口」义扩展到工程领域。

items.en: The secret-plan sense of hatching off /hatching up a scheme appears.
items.cn: 十六七世纪出现了「暗中策划」的用法，如 hatch up a scheme。

items.en: The hatchback car takes the word for its rear lid, and hatchery names the industrial version of the bird sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中，掀背车以后盖沿用 hatch 一词，孵化场则用 hatchery 指工业化孵化。

note.en: Group one gathers the hatch word family and the egg field; group two gathers verbs of secret planning.
note.cn: 第一组是 hatch 词族与「蛋」的语义场；第二组是表示密谋计划的动词。

entries.definition: a place where eggs are kept warm and young fish or birds are raised
entries.definitionCN: 把蛋保温并培育幼鱼的场所，即孵化场

entries.definition: a car whose rear door is a large upward-opening lid called a hatch
entries.definitionCN: 后门是一整块向上掀起后盖的汽车，后盖即 hatch

entries.definition: Roof covering made of straw; it looks close to hatch but comes from a different root, so spelling only.
entries.definitionCN: 用稻草铺成的屋顶；拼写与 hatch 相近，但词源不同，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: to sit on eggs, or to think constantly about an unhappy idea
entries.definitionCN: 孵蛋，或反复思索不快的念头

entries.definition: to make a secret plan, usually the noun of the plot that is hatched
entries.definitionCN: 暗中策划，常与 hatch 搭配成「策划阴谋」

entries.definition: to keep eggs or bacteria at a warm, steady temperature so they develop
entries.definitionCN: 把蛋或细菌保持在稳定的温暖环境中使其发育

entries.definition: to keep animals so that they produce young, a wider process than hatching
entries.definitionCN: 饲养动物使其繁殖，范围比「孵化」更广

normalIntro.en: Hatch links a bird breaking out of a shell with a secret that suddenly comes out of hiding.
normalIntro.cn: hatch 把「小鸟破壳而出」与「秘密突然现身」连在一起。

normal.en: The past form is simply hatched for both the bird and the plot.
normal.cn: 鸟与阴谋的过去式都是 hatched。

normal.en: Hatch a plan and hatch eggs share one idea: something grows inside before it appears.
normal.cn: 「酝酿计划」与「孵蛋」共享同一意象：东西先在里面长成，再露面。

normal.en: Hatchback keeps the opening sense alive in modern cars.
normal.cn: hatchback 让「开口」义在现代汽车中延续。

normal.en: The opposite of hatch out is stay inside the shell, so hatching always means coming out.
normal.cn: hatch out 的反面是留在壳里，所以「孵化」总含有「出来」的意思。

normal.en: The phrase escape hatch is a door in an emergency and also a way out of a problem.
normal.cn: escape hatch 既是紧急出口，也是摆脱困境的办法。

abstract.en: Picture a shell cracking from the inside, with a tiny beak pushing through.
abstract.cn: 想象蛋壳从里面裂开，一只小喙顶了出来。

abstract.en: Imagine four people whispering around a table under a single lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象四个人在一盏灯下围着桌子低声商量。

abstract.en: See a car boot lid springing open in the rain.
abstract.cn: 眼前浮现雨中汽车后盖弹开的画面。

examples.en: The turtle eggs hatched after two warm months.
examples.cn: 海龟蛋在温暖的两个月后孵化了。

examples.en: They hatched a clever plan to save the library.
examples.cn: 他们商量出一个保住图书馆的巧妙计划。

examples.en: The stowaway was found hiding below the hatch.
examples.cn: 偷渡者被发现藏在小门的下方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈七」——数到七就破壳，七只小鸟一起孵化；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hæccan（孵化）＋hæc／hæcc（小门、舱口，来自表示「门」的词）；两者均为本族日耳曼源词，无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Hatch starts with the physical breaking of a shell, gives its opening verbs both a secret-plan and a production field, and then names real openings in decks, floors, and cars.
sensesIntro.cn: hatch 从蛋壳破裂的实体动作出发，一方面延伸到暗中策划与悄悄孕育，一方面用名词指甲板、地板与车辆上的真实开口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack spreading on a shell, then a small head pushing out.
core.cn: 核心意象：壳上裂开细缝，一只小脑袋顶了出来。

branches.en: Keeping eggs warm is the human or animal action.
branches.cn: 为蛋保温，是人或动物一方的动作。

branches.en: The young creature breaking out is the same event seen from inside.
branches.cn: 幼体破壳而出，是同一事件从内部看的样子。

branches.en: Things hidden until they appear become secret plans.
branches.cn: 由藏到露的过程，被用来形容秘密计划。

branches.en: From the separate door word, a deck opening and a car lid both take the name.
branches.cn: 同一个表示「门」的词源，又派生出甲板开口与汽车后盖的名称。

branches.en: A plot and a quiet workshop both produce something before it shows.
branches.cn: 阴谋与安静的作坊，都在成果现身之前先孕育它。

intro.en: Hatch is a native English word, and its family grows with -ery, -ing, and -ling.
intro.cn: hatch 是本族英语词，其词族靠 -ery、-ing 与 -ling 扩展。

latinIntro.en: No Latin form stands behind hatch, but ova, pullus, and cavea show Latin could express eggs, chicks, and openings.
latinIntro.cn: hatch 背后没有拉丁语形式，但 ova、pullus、cavea 显示拉丁语可用别的词表达「蛋、雏、开口」。

items.example: The Old English verb gives the bird sense its base.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词为「鸟」的义项提供基础。

items.example: Hæcc supplies the opening sense.
items.exampleCN: hæcc 提供了「开口」义。

items.meaning: a place where something is done
items.example: The suffix forms hatchery.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 hatchery。

items.meaning: a place where eggs are incubated
items.example: A fish hatchery releases young fish upstream.
items.exampleCN: 鱼类孵化场会把幼鱼放流到上游。

items.meaning: the action of hatching, or a shading of lines
items.meaningCN: 孵化这一动作，或排线阴影
items.example: Hatching describes the breaking of eggs and cross-hatched drawing.
items.exampleCN: hatching 既指孵化，也指交叉排线的画法。

items.example: The suffix forms hatchling.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 hatchling。

items.example: Hatchlings head straight for the sea.
items.exampleCN: 刚孵出的小海龟直奔大海。

items.example: The compound forms hatchback.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合成分构成 hatchback。

items.example: The submarine crew used the escape hatch.
items.exampleCN: 潜艇船员使用了逃生舱口。

definition_zh: 拖；拉；用力拽；运输；运送物；(一次捕获的)收获；(一次偷得的)赃物
definition_en: to pull something heavy with effort; also the load carried, the catch or profit gained in one attempt
core_image: 一个人弯着腰，用绳索把沉重的箱子一寸寸拖过地面
scene: 渔网从海里被拉上来，网里全是银色的鱼。The fishermen hauled the net onto the deck and sorted the silver fish.
sceneCN: 这里 haul 是「用力拖、拉」（第 1 个义项：把重物费力拖拽）；句意：渔民们把渔网拖上甲板，分拣那些银色的鱼。

pos.zh: 拖运；一次捕获量；(偷得的)赃物；距离

collocations.zh: 长途运输；长期而艰苦的过程

derivatives.zh: 由 haul 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「拖运者；运输公司」
由 haul 加后缀 -age 构成，义为「拖运；货运」
英式写法，由 haul 加后缀 -ier 构成，义为「货运公司」

senses.title: To drag something heavy
senses.definition: to pull something heavy slowly and with great effort
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而费力地拖动沉重的东西
senses.example: They hauled the log out of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把圆木从河里拖了出来。
senses.why: The word enters English from French haler, to pull or drag, and keeps that physical act at its centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自法语 haler（拉、拖），一直把「用力拖拽重物」这一身体动作放在核心。

senses.title: To transport goods
senses.definition: to carry goods or loads from one place to another, especially by road or rail
senses.definitionCN: 把货物或载荷从一个地方运到另一个地方，尤指陆路运输
senses.example: Trucks haul coal from the mine to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车把煤从矿井运到港口。
senses.why: Transport means dragging a heavy load behind you, so the moving sense grew naturally from the pulling sense.
senses.whyCN: 运输本来就是「把重载拖在身后」，所以位移义从拖拽义自然生长出来。

senses.title: A load or quantity carried
senses.definition: the amount of something carried or brought in at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次运送或带回的量
senses.example: A haul of timber filled the whole trailer.
senses.exampleCN: 一整车的木材把拖车装满了。
senses.why: The noun names the result of the pulling action, namely whatever comes back on the truck or in the net.
senses.whyCN: 名词义指拖拽动作的结果，也就是卡车拉回或网里捞上来的那一堆东西。

senses.title: A catch of fish
senses.definition: the number of fish or animals caught or taken in one trip
senses.definitionCN: 一次出海或捕猎所获得的鱼或动物的数量
senses.example: This year the fishing fleet reported a poor haul.
senses.exampleCN: 今年渔船队报告的捕获量很差。
senses.why: Fishing is pulling nets through water, so one haul of the net becomes one catch.
senses.whyCN: 捕鱼就是把网从水里拖出来，所以一次收网就成了「一网之获」。

senses.title: Stolen goods or loot
senses.definition: the goods or money stolen or gained by criminals in one incident
senses.definitionCN: 罪犯在一次作案中偷得或得到的货物与钱财
senses.example: The thieves escaped with a haul worth thousands of pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 窃贼带着价值数千英镑的赃物逃走了。
senses.why: Thieves drag their loot away, so the drag-noun came to mean a whole batch of stolen goods.
senses.whyCN: 盗贼会把赃物拖走，于是这个表示「拖运之物」的名词就指一整批赃物。

senses.title: A distance to travel
senses.definition: a distance travelled, especially a long or difficult one
senses.definitionCN: 一段路程，尤指漫长或艰难的行程
senses.example: The cabin is still a long haul from the nearest town.
senses.exampleCN: 这间小屋离最近的城镇还有很长一段路。
senses.why: A haul is one stretch of dragging a load, so it widens to any distance of travel.
senses.whyCN: 一次 haul 是拖着负载走的一段路，于是引申为任意一段行程的距离。

senses.title: A long difficult effort
senses.definition: a long, hard period of effort to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为达到目标而经历的长期艰苦努力
senses.example: Recovering the factory will be a long haul.
senses.exampleCN: 让这家工厂恢复元气将是一段漫长的过程。
senses.why: The travel distance becomes an effort when the trip is long, giving the abstract sense of a hard slog.
senses.whyCN: 行程一长就变成苦熬，因此抽象出「长期艰苦过程」的含义。

senses.title: To pull up before a court
senses.definition: to bring someone forcibly before a court or an authority to answer for a wrong
senses.definitionCN: 强行把某人带到法庭或当局面前问罪
senses.example: The company was hauled before the court for polluting the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司因污染河流而被送上法庭。
senses.why: Legal use keeps the physical dragging, with the person now dragged toward a judge.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法保留了「拖」的身体动作，只是被拖拽的对象换成了被带到法官面前的人。

intro.en: Haul comes from Old French haler, to pull or drag, itself from a Germanic verb family.
intro.cn: haul 来自古法语 haler（拉、拖），其源头一般认为属于日耳曼语族的一类动词。

items.en: A Germanic grabbing and pulling verb family, generally assumed as the distant source.
items.cn: 一般认为源头是日耳曼语族表示「抓住并拉扯」的一组动词。

items.en: Haler means to draw or drag a boat or load.
items.cn: 古法语 haler 意为拉船、拖载。

items.en: Haulen appears in English with the sense of pulling a net or cargo.
items.cn: 中古英语 haulen 出现，指拉网或拖运货物。

items.en: Nautical and mining trades spread the word to fishing catches and goods transport.
items.cn: 航海与采矿行当把这个词推广到捕鱼收获与货物运输。

items.en: The noun extends to stolen goods, travel distance, and long hard efforts.
items.cn: 名词义扩展到赃物、行程距离与长期艰苦的过程。

note.en: Haul sits among words of dragging, from the base verb to its transport nouns, and close to drag and tow.
note.cn: haul 处于「拖拽」词群中，上有基础动词与运输名词，旁边是 drag、tow 这类近义词。

entries.definition: the transport of goods by road or rail
entries.definitionCN: 货运；拖运费

entries.definition: a company that transports goods, British use
entries.definitionCN: 货运公司（英式用法）

entries.definition: strong and healthy, an adjective with an unrelated origin
entries.definitionCN: 强健的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to pull something along the ground with effort
entries.definitionCN: 沿地面费力地拖

entries.definition: to pull a vehicle behind another
entries.definitionCN: 拖曳；牵引

entries.definition: to hold and take something somewhere in your hands or arms
entries.definitionCN: 搬运；携带

normalIntro.en: Haul is a rope in your hands and a heavy load behind you.
normalIntro.cn: haul 是手里攥着绳子、身后拖着重物。

normal.en: To haul something is to pull it hard and slowly.
normal.cn: haul something 就是用力而缓慢地把它拖走。

normal.en: Trucks haul goods over long distances.
normal.cn: 卡车长途运货，用的就是这个「拖运」意象。

normal.en: A good haul means a big catch or a big looting.
normal.cn: a good haul 指一次大丰收或一大笔赃物。

normal.en: The long haul is the hard part of any project.
normal.cn: the long haul 就是任何项目中最艰难的那一段。

normal.en: Compare drag and tow: haul stresses the weight and distance of a load.
normal.cn: 对比 drag 与 tow：haul 更强调负重与长距离。

abstract.en: See a rope taut as a heavy crate slides over stone.
abstract.cn: 想象绳索绷紧，沉重的箱子在石面上滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a fleet of lorries carrying coal down a mountain road.
abstract.cn: 想象一队卡车沿着山路运送煤炭。

abstract.en: Think of a net bursting with fish as it comes up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张装满鱼的网被拽上来。

examples.en: Volunteers hauled sandbags to the flooded street.
examples.cn: 志愿者把沙袋拖到被淹的街道上。

examples.en: The robbery netted the gang a haul of illegal weapons.
examples.cn: 这次抢劫让这伙人得到了一批非法武器。

examples.en: It is a long haul from the airport to the mountain village.
examples.cn: 从机场到山村是一段很长的路程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嚎」——拖着沉箱子上坡，累得直嚎；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 haler（拉、拖）→ 中古英语 haulen（拉网、拖货）→ 英语 haul，核心义「拽着重物走」。

sensesIntro.en: Haul begins with dragging a heavy load, extends to carrying goods, then names the catch, the loot, the distance, and finally a long hard effort.
sensesIntro.cn: haul 从「拖拽重物」出发，延伸到「运货」，再名词化为捕获量、赃物、路程距离，最后抽象为长期艰苦的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulling a heavy crate across the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子把沉重的箱子拖过地面。

branches.en: Dragging a heavy thing is the physical core.
branches.cn: 拖拽重物是身体层面的核心。

branches.en: Transport extends the pull to goods moving between places.
branches.cn: 运输义把「拖」扩展到货物在两地之间移动。

branches.en: One hauls a crate, or a company is hauled before a judge.
branches.cn: 可以拖一只箱子，也可以把一家公司押上法庭。

branches.en: The load, the catch, and the loot are all what one haul brings back.
branches.cn: 运输量、捕获量与赃物都是「一趟拖回来」的东西。

branches.en: A long distance of travel becomes a long, hard effort.
branches.cn: 漫长的路程进而成为漫长艰苦的努力。

intro.en: Haul is a simple verb with no Latin prefix, and its family is built with English noun suffixes.
intro.cn: haul 是不带拉丁前缀的单纯动词，它的词族主要靠英语名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the closest old relatives are Germanic and Old French forms.
latinIntro.cn: haul 没有拉丁词源，最接近的旧亲属是日耳曼语与古法语的形式。

items.example: Haul keeps the drag image alive.
items.exampleCN: haul 保留了拖拽的意象。

items.meaning: a person or firm that hauls
items.example: The suffix -er adds an agent.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 加上施事者。

items.example: Haulier uses a French-style agent ending.
items.exampleCN: haulier 使用法语式的施事后缀。

items.example: The suffix -age forms haulage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 构成 haulage。

items.meaning: hauling or the money paid for it
items.example: Haulage names the dragging trade.
items.exampleCN: haulage 指拖运这一行当。

items.meaning: a long distance or a hard period
items.example: Long haul turns distance into effort.
items.exampleCN: long haul 把距离转化为努力。

items.example: Overhaul pulls a boat up for repair.
items.exampleCN: overhaul 原指把船拉上岸检修。

items.example: Haul up adds a direction of motion.
items.exampleCN: haul up 加上了向上的方向。

definition_zh: （鬼魂）萦绕；常出没；纠缠；萦绕心头；常去的地方
definition_en: to visit a place frequently, or to keep coming back to a person or mind like a ghost
core_image: 一座空屋窗前，晃动的影子每晚都回到同一间房
scene: 老宅里的人说，每到午夜，楼上的影子就会再次出现。Locals say a pale figure haunts the old house on the hill every night.
sceneCN: 这里 haunt 是「出没、萦绕」（第 1 个义项：鬼魂或形象反复回到某处）；句意：当地人说，一个苍白的身影每晚都在山上那座老宅里出没。

pos.zh: 常去的地方；经常光顾之处

collocations.zh: 多年来萦绕在某人脑中

derivatives.zh: 由 haunt 加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「闹鬼的；挥之不去的」
由 haunt 加后缀 -ing 构成，义为「萦绕心头的；难忘的」
由 haunt 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「常出没者」

senses.title: To appear in a place again and again
senses.definition: for a ghost or a strange image to keep appearing in the same place
senses.definitionCN: 指鬼魂或奇异形象在同一地点不断出现
senses.example: People say her spirit still haunts the chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 人们说她的灵魂仍在教堂里出没。
senses.why: The word is most likely a Germanic verb for going often to a place, and ghosts are the visitors who never stop going back.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这个词源自古英语中表示「常去、惯于往来」的日耳曼语动词，而鬼魂正是永不停止归来的到访者。

senses.title: To keep troubling your mind
senses.definition: for a memory, fear, or image to keep returning to your thoughts
senses.definitionCN: 指记忆、恐惧或画面不断回到你的脑际
senses.example: The look on his face haunted me for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上的表情困扰了我好几周。
senses.why: A memory that keeps coming back behaves like a ghost returning to the same room.
senses.whyCN: 反复浮现的记忆就像鬼魂回到同一间屋子，于是 haunt 从「出没」转为「在脑中萦绕」。

senses.title: To go to a place often
senses.definition: to visit or spend time in a place regularly
senses.definitionCN: 经常去某个地方或在那里消磨时间
senses.example: As a student, he haunted the city library.
senses.exampleCN: 学生时代，他常泡在市图书馆里。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, a frequent visitor who keeps coming back by habit.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：出于习惯反复前来的常客。

senses.title: To follow someone persistently
senses.definition: to stay so close to a person that it cannot be shaken off
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟着某人，使其无法摆脱
senses.example: Doubts haunted her before every exam.
senses.exampleCN: 每次考试前，疑虑都纠缠着她。
senses.why: Persistence is the shadow of the return: whatever keeps coming back can also keep following you.
senses.whyCN: 「反复归来」的阴影就是「纠缠」：会一再出现的东西，也会一直跟着你。

senses.title: A place you often visit
senses.definition: a place that someone visits often
senses.definitionCN: 某人经常去的地方
senses.example: They met again in one of their old haunts.
senses.exampleCN: 他们又在一处旧日常去的酒馆里相遇了。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the place that calls the regular visitor back.
senses.whyCN: 动词名词化，就指那个总把常客召回来的地方。

senses.title: A place with supernatural visitors
senses.definition: a place that ghosts or spirits are said to visit
senses.definitionCN: 据说有鬼魂或精灵出没的地方
senses.example: The mill is a haunt for curious teenagers at night.
senses.exampleCN: 这座磨坊夜里成了好奇的青少年聚集出没的地方。
senses.why: The noun keeps the supernatural overtone and names a site where visitations are expected.
senses.whyCN: 名词义保留了超自然色彩，指被预期会有「到访者」的地方。

senses.title: To keep returning as a problem
senses.definition: for an old problem or debt to come back and affect you again
senses.definitionCN: 指旧问题或债务再度回来影响某人
senses.example: The results of that shortcut came back to haunt the engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 那个走捷径的后果回过头来缠上了这些工程师。
senses.why: An unsolved problem, like a ghost, refuses to stay in the past and returns to the present.
senses.whyCN: 未解决的问题像鬼魂一样不肯留在过去，总要回到当下。

intro.en: Haunt is usually traced to Old French hanter, to frequent a place, itself probably from a Germanic verb.
intro.cn: haunt 一般认为源自法语动词 hanter（常去某处），后者很可能又来自日耳曼语动词。

items.en: A Germanic verb for going home or keeping to a place is the likely root.
items.cn: 可能的源头是一个表示「回家、待在某处」的日耳曼语动词。

items.en: Hanter means to frequent a place or associate with someone.
items.cn: 古法语 hanter 意为常去某地、与某人交往。

items.en: Haunten enters English with the sense of resorting to a place often.
items.cn: 中古英语 haunten 进入英语，意为「经常前往某地」。

items.en: With stories of spirits, the word takes on the ghostly sense of visiting the living.
items.cn: 随着鬼怪故事流行，这个词获得了「鬼魂造访活人」的灵异含义。

items.en: The mind sense extends from visiting to obsessing, and the noun names favourite places.
items.cn: 现代英语由「造访」引申到「在脑中萦绕」，名词义则指钟爱之地。

note.en: Haunt shares the frequent-visit root with jaunt and daunt look-alikes, and sits near words for repeated visits.
note.cn: haunt 与 jaunt、daunt 只是形近，另有常去与纠缠意义的近义邻词。

entries.definition: visited by ghosts, or filled with unhappy memories
entries.definitionCN: 闹鬼的；充满不愉快回忆的

entries.definition: to make someone lose confidence
entries.definitionCN: 使气馁；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a short trip for pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 短途游览；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to visit a place often
entries.definitionCN: 常去；光顾

entries.definition: to fill a persons mind completely
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷；使无法摆脱

entries.definition: to cause continual trouble to a person
entries.definitionCN: 不断困扰；折磨

normalIntro.en: Haunt means coming back: a ghost, a memory, or a habit that keeps returning.
normalIntro.cn: haunt 的核心是「又回来了」：鬼魂、记忆或习惯一再回到原处。

normal.en: To be haunted by something is to be troubled by it constantly.
normal.cn: be haunted by something 就是被某事持续困扰。

normal.en: A haunted house is a house ghosts keep visiting.
normal.cn: a haunted house 就是鬼魂不断造访的房子。

normal.en: Old haunts are the places you used to go to often.
normal.cn: old haunts 是你过去常去的地方。

normal.en: A problem can come back to haunt you later.
normal.cn: 一个问题日后可能回过头来缠上你。

normal.en: Compare inhabit and frequent: haunt adds the feeling of returning again and again.
normal.cn: 对比 inhabit 与 frequent：haunt 多了一层「一次又一次回来」的感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain moving at a window where nobody stands.
abstract.cn: 想象无人站立的窗前，窗帘自己在动。

abstract.en: Hear an old song playing again in an empty hall.
abstract.cn: 想象空荡的大厅里又响起一首老歌。

abstract.en: See the same regular guest back at the same corner table.
abstract.cn: 想象同一位常客又坐回同一个角落的位子。

examples.en: The memory of the crash still haunts the survivors.
examples.cn: 车祸的记忆至今仍萦绕在幸存者心头。

examples.en: They spent the evening in an old haunt near the station.
examples.cn: 他们在车站附近一处旧日常去的地方消磨了一个晚上。

examples.en: Bad decisions made today may return to haunt the city.
examples.cn: 今天做出的糟糕决定，日后可能回过头来困扰这座城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嚎」——鬼魂半夜出来嚎叫，反复吓人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 日耳曼语动词「回家、待在某处」（推测）→ 古法语 hanter（常去、交往）→ 中古英语 haunten → 英语 haunt，核心义「一再回到同一处」。

sensesIntro.en: Haunt starts as a spirit returning to a place, spreads to memories and doubts returning to the mind, and ends as the favoured place of a frequent visitor.
sensesIntro.cn: haunt 从「精灵反复回到某处」起步，扩散到「记忆与疑虑在脑中反复出现」，最后名词化为常客钟爱之地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shadow that returns to the same window every night.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子每晚都回到同一扇窗前。

branches.en: A ghost repeatedly appearing is the vivid core.
branches.cn: 鬼魂反复出现是最鲜明的核心义。

branches.en: A memory that keeps returning moves the scene indoors into the mind.
branches.cn: 不断回来的记忆把场景从屋外搬进了脑海。

branches.en: The habitual visitor and the clingy follower share the habit of returning.
branches.cn: 习惯性访客与甩不掉的追随者都共享「一再回来」的特点。

branches.en: The noun names the place that calls people or spirits back.
branches.cn: 名词义指那个把人或鬼魂唤回的地方。

branches.en: Old trouble in the mind and old trouble in life both refuse to stay past.
branches.cn: 心里的旧忧与生活中的旧账都不肯留在过去。

intro.en: Haunt has no Latin prefix, and its English family uses -ed, -ing, and -er endings.
intro.cn: haunt 没有拉丁前缀，英语词族靠 -ed、-ing、-er 这类词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin field supplies no direct ancestor; the nearest older form is French hanter, of Germanic origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有直接祖先词，最接近的旧形式是源自日耳曼语的法语 hanter。

items.meaning: to keep returning to a place or mind
items.example: Haunt keeps the return image.
items.exampleCN: haunt 保留了「回来」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms haunted.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 haunted。

items.example: Haunted describes a house with visitors.
items.exampleCN: haunted 描述有「访客」的房子。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms haunting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 haunting。

items.example: Haunting describes a vivid memory.
items.exampleCN: haunting 形容难忘的画面。

items.example: The suffix -er forms haunter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 haunter。

items.example: Haunter is a rare agent noun.
items.exampleCN: haunter 是一个少见的施事名词。

items.example: Old haunts uses the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: old haunts 用的是名词义。

definition_zh: 鹰；隼；鹰派人物；推销；兜售；清嗓子；(放鹰)纵鹰捕猎
definition_en: a sharp-eyed bird of prey; also a person who pushes a hard line, and the act of selling goods in the street
core_image: 高空盘旋的猛禽猛地收拢翅膀，俯冲而下
scene: 集市上有人边走边喊，向路人推销他的货物。A young man stood at the market gate, hawking cheap watches to anyone who walked past.
sceneCN: 这里 hawk 是「沿街兜售、叫卖」（第 4 个义项：大声推销商品）；句意：一个年轻人站在市场门口，向每个路过的人兜售廉价手表。

pos.zh: 兜售；推销；清嗓子；纵鹰捕猎

derivatives.zh: 由 hawk 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「小贩；沿街兜售者」
由 hawk 加后缀 -ing 构成，义为「放鹰捕猎；鹰猎」
由 hawk 加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「鹰派的；主战的」

senses.title: A bird of prey
senses.definition: a bird with a short hooked bill that hunts small animals and flies very fast
senses.definitionCN: 一种喙短而带钩、捕食小动物、飞行极快的猛禽
senses.example: A hawk circled above the field before it dived.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鹰在田野上空盘旋，然后俯冲而下。
senses.why: The word enters English from Old English hafoc, a name for these fierce hunting birds.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古英语 hafoc，本来就是这类凶猛猎鸟的名字。

senses.title: A person with a keen eye
senses.definition: someone who notices details fast, often used in the phrase hawk-eyed
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速察觉细节的人，常出现在 hawk-eyed 这一说法中
senses.example: The hawk-eyed editor caught every typo.
senses.exampleCN: 那位目光锐利的编辑挑出了每一处拼写错误。
senses.why: Hawks spot tiny prey from far above, so their sharp sight becomes a figure for careful attention.
senses.whyCN: 鹰能从高空发现小小的猎物，于是它的锐利视力成为「细致观察」的比喻。

senses.title: An advocate of war
senses.definition: a person or politician who supports aggressive or military solutions
senses.definitionCN: 支持强硬或军事手段的人或政治家
senses.example: The war hawk urged the cabinet to send troops.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主战派力促内阁出兵。
senses.why: The raptor that strikes first lends its name to the politician who reaches for force.
senses.whyCN: 先发制人的猛禽，把名字借给了主张动用武力的政治家。

senses.title: To sell goods in the street
senses.definition: to offer goods for sale in public, often loudly or persistently
senses.definitionCN: 在公共场所出售货物，往往大声或执著地推销
senses.example: Street traders hawk fruit from wooden carts.
senses.exampleCN: 街头小贩在木车上叫卖水果。
senses.why: This selling verb is linked to itinerant pedlars and is often assumed to share the bird name, from a trader who hovers around buyers.
senses.whyCN: 这个卖货的动词与流动小贩有关，通常认为它借用了鸟名，因为小贩像鹰一样在买主身边盘旋。

senses.title: To clear your throat noisily
senses.definition: to cough or clear the throat with a loud rasping sound
senses.definitionCN: 用响亮而粗厉的声音咳嗽或清清嗓子
senses.example: He hawked loudly before starting the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 他在开始演讲前大声清了清嗓子。
senses.why: The imitative verb of hacking and coughing is spelled alike and has merged into the hawk word family.
senses.whyCN: 模仿咳嗽声的动词拼写相同，被认为是拟声来源，如今被视为 hawk 词族的一部分。

senses.title: To hunt with a trained hawk
senses.definition: to hunt game using a trained hawk, a sport called falconry
senses.definitionCN: 用训练过的鹰打猎，这种运动叫放鹰狩猎
senses.example: The duke hawked on the moors every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵每年秋天都在荒原上放鹰捕猎。
senses.why: The verb is simply the bird name turned into an activity, as with many animal nouns.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把鸟名转成了活动，许多动物名词都有这种用法。

senses.title: To spread gossip and news
senses.definition: to pass on information, often gossip, quickly from person to person
senses.definitionCN: 把消息或闲话迅速从一个人传给另一个人
senses.example: News of the merger was hawked about the office within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 合并的消息几分钟内就在办公室里传开了。
senses.why: Street sellers shout their news, so the selling sense widens to spreading talk far and wide.
senses.whyCN: 街边商贩会大声叫喊消息，于是兜售义扩展为把闲话传得满城皆知。

intro.en: Hawk the bird descends from Old English hafoc, and the throat-clearing verb is an imitative word that came to share the spelling.
intro.cn: 鸟名 hawk 出自古英语 hafoc（猎鹰），而「清嗓子」的动词是拟声词，后来才与它拼写相同。

items.en: Hafoc names the sharp-eyed hunting bird.
items.cn: 古英语 hafoc 指那种目光锐利的猎鸟。

items.en: The form shifts towards the modern hawk, and falconry spreads the bird sense.
items.cn: 词形逐渐演变为现代的 hawk，放鹰狩猎使鸟名广为人知。

items.en: The sold-by-shouting verb sets out with itinerant pedlars, generally assumed to be linked to the bird.
items.cn: 沿街叫卖的动词随流动小贩出现，通常认为与鸟名相关。

items.en: Political writers turn the fierce bird into a nickname for supporters of force.
items.cn: 政治作家把猛禽借作主张武力者的绰号。

items.en: The hawk name covers a keen eye, a hard line in politics, and loud street sales.
items.cn: 现代英语中 hawk 涵盖锐利眼光、强硬政治立场与街头叫卖。

note.en: Hawk is both a raptor and a verb of hard selling, close to other birds of prey and to the words it merges with in spelling.
note.cn: hawk 既是猛禽名，又是高声推销的动词，它与其它猛禽及拼写相近的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who sells goods in the street
entries.definitionCN: 沿街叫卖的小贩

entries.definition: to pawn something, or the joint of an animal leg
entries.definitionCN: 典当；动物后腿关节；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an ablative phrase in Latin, not an English noun
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的介词短语；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a fast hunting bird trained to catch prey
entries.definitionCN: 隼；被训练捕猎的猛禽

entries.definition: a very large powerful bird of prey
entries.definitionCN: 鹰；雕

entries.definition: to sell goods while travelling from place to place
entries.definitionCN: 流动兜售；沿街叫卖

normalIntro.en: Hawk is first a bird that strikes from the sky, then anyone or anything that presses forward like one.
normalIntro.cn: hawk 首先是自天而降的猛禽，其次是像它一样咄咄逼进的人或事。

normal.en: Hawk-eyed means having very sharp sight.
normal.cn: hawk-eyed 表示目光非常锐利。

normal.en: To watch like a hawk is to watch without blinking.
normal.cn: watch like a hawk 就是一眨不眨地紧盯。

normal.en: A war hawk wants a quick military reply.
normal.cn: a war hawk 主张迅速以军事手段回应。

normal.en: To hawk goods is to shout them out in a market.
normal.cn: hawk goods 就是在市场里大声叫卖货物。

normal.en: Compare falcon and eagle: hawk is the broadest everyday name for these birds.
normal.cn: 对比 falcon 与 eagle：hawk 是这类鸟最通俗、涵盖最广的叫法。

abstract.en: See a wing snap shut as the bird drops from the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象猛禽从天空坠落时翅膀猛地一收。

abstract.en: Think of the smallest mouse moving in tall grass seen from high above.
abstract.cn: 想象从高空望见草丛里一动的小老鼠。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pushing a politician toward a war room.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人把一个政治家推向作战会议室的画面。

examples.en: The farmer guarded his chickens against hawks.
examples.cn: 农夫保护他的鸡不受鹰的伤害。

examples.en: She kept a hawk eye on the two small children.
examples.cn: 她紧紧盯着那两个小孩。

examples.en: Street sellers hawk souvenirs near the museum gate.
examples.cn: 街头小贩在博物馆门口叫卖纪念品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嚎」——商贩沿街嚎叫卖货，像鹰一样盯住顾客；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hafoc（猎鹰）→ 中古英语 hawk → 英语 hawk；鸟名「目光锐利、俯冲猛击」的形象又派生出鹰派与叫卖义。

sensesIntro.en: Hawk starts with the raptor, transfers its sharp eye and fierce habits to people, and turns into verbs of shouting sales while the throat-clearing sense sits beside it.
sensesIntro.cn: hawk 从猛禽起步，把锐利目光与凶猛习性转借给人物，再变成大声叫卖的动词，清嗓子义则并列在旁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raptor folding its wings and diving.
core.cn: 核心意象：猛禽收拢双翅俯冲而下。

branches.en: The hunting bird is the concrete centre.
branches.cn: 猎鸟是具体的核心。

branches.en: Its sharp sight becomes a figure for keen attention.
branches.cn: 它锐利的视力成为细致观察的比喻。

branches.en: Its readiness to strike becomes a name for advocates of force.
branches.cn: 它随时出击的习性成为主张武力者的代称。

branches.en: Loud street selling and gossip spreading share the shouting trader.
branches.cn: 沿街叫卖与传闲话都共享那个高声叫喊的小贩形象。

branches.en: Throat clearing and hunting with a bird are two separate verbs dressed in the same word.
branches.cn: 清嗓子与放鹰捕猎是两个同形却来源不同的动词。

intro.en: Hawk is a Germanic bird name; the Latin section lists no direct ancestor, only the English endings that build its family.
intro.cn: hawk 是日耳曼语的鸟名，没有拉丁直接祖先，只有构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source stands behind hawk; the closest classical relatives belong to terms for falcons, not to hawk itself.
latinIntro.cn: hawk 没有拉丁词源，古典语里最接近的是指隼类的词，而非 hawk 本身。

items.example: Hawk is the broad everyday bird name.
items.exampleCN: hawk 是这类鸟最通俗的名字。

items.example: The suffix -er forms hawker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 hawker。

items.example: Hawker is the seller of the verb.
items.exampleCN: hawker 是那个动词的施事者。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms hawking.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 hawking。

items.meaning: the sport of hunting with hawks
items.example: Hawking names the old sport.
items.exampleCN: hawking 指这项古老的运动。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms hawkish.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 构成 hawkish。

items.example: Hawkish turns the bird into a policy label.
items.exampleCN: hawkish 把鸟名变成了政策标签。

items.example: Hawk-eyed joins the bird to the eye.
items.exampleCN: hawk-eyed 把鸟和眼睛连在一起。

definition_zh: 山楂；山楂树；山楂属的灌木或小乔木
definition_en: a small thorny tree with white or pink flowers, red berries called haws, and hard sharp thorns
core_image: 春天开满白花、秋天挂满红果的小树，枝条上长着坚硬的刺
scene: 篱笆边的山楂树在五月开花，到了秋天枝头结满红果。Every spring the village hedge turns white as the hawthorn blossoms along the lane.
sceneCN: 这里 hawthorn 是「山楂树」（第 1 个义项：开白花、结红果且带刺的小树）；句意为每年春天，村道旁的树篱都会因山楂树开花而一片雪白。

derivatives.zh: 由「山楂」的原形加 thorn 构成整体词，haw 本身指山楂果，现多见于方言与鸟类名称
由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「像山楂一样多刺的；长满山楂的」
由本词加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「长有山楂树的」，多见于描写树篱或田野的文本

senses.title: A thorny flowering tree
senses.definition: a small tree or bush of the rose family, with lobed leaves, white or pink five-petalled flowers and long hard thorns
senses.definitionCN: 蔷薇科的小乔木或灌木，叶片分裂，开白或粉红色的五瓣花，枝上有长而坚硬的刺
senses.example: The hawthorn flowered early this year, before the apples.
senses.exampleCN: 今年山楂树开得早，比苹果树还早。
senses.why: The first half of the name is simply the word haw, the old English name for its fruit; the two parts were joined into one word because haw by itself had become too vague to name a plant.
senses.whyCN: 名字的前半就是 haw，那是古英语里对这种果实的称呼；因为单说 haw 已不足以指认这种植物，两部分才合成一个词。

senses.title: The fruit of the bush
senses.definition: the small red fruit of the hawthorn, known as a haw, used in jellies and some medicines
senses.definitionCN: 山楂树结的小红果，称为 haw，可用于制作果冻和部分药物
senses.example: In autumn the branches hang heavy with red haws after the hawthorn berries ripen.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天山楂果成熟后，枝条被红色的果子压得低垂。
senses.why: Because one word now covered both the tree and its crop, English speakers use hawthorn for the plant and haw or hawthorn berry for the fruit it bears.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个合起来的词同时指树和果实，英语里就用 hawthorn 说植物，用 haw 或 hawthorn berry 说它结的果。

senses.title: A boundary hedge
senses.definition: a dense row of hawthorns planted to mark a boundary, keep animals in and screen a field
senses.definitionCN: 成排种植的密实山楂树，用来标示地界、圈住牲畜并遮挡田地
senses.example: Farmers laid a hawthorn hedge to fence the new pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 农人们修剪、编扎了一道山楂树篱，把新牧场的边界圈起来。
senses.why: The plant grows dense and thorny in a few years, so country people planted rows of it along field edges, and the tree became a living wall.
senses.whyCN: 这种植物几年内就长得密实又多刺，乡间便沿田埂成排栽种，于是树成了会生长的墙。

senses.title: A flowering sign of Beltaine
senses.definition: a plant whose white May blossoms mark the turn to summer in old British and Irish custom
senses.definitionCN: 在英国与爱尔兰旧俗中，以白色五月的花标记入夏时节的植物
senses.example: Villagers once decked their doorways with hawthorn on the first of May.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时村民会在五月初一用山楂枝装饰门口。
senses.why: Its blossom opens around the start of May, so British and Irish custom tied the tree to the beginning of summer, and it appears in May Day and Beltaine celebrations.
senses.whyCN: 它在五月初前后开花，英国与爱尔兰的习俗因此把这棵树和入夏连在一起，它也出现在五月节与迎夏节的庆典里。

senses.title: A symbol of the sacred
senses.definition: a tree regarded with awe in folklore, said to shelter fairies and unlucky to cut down alone
senses.definitionCN: 民俗中被敬畏的树，据说为精灵所居，独自砍伐会招来不吉
senses.example: Old stories warn of bad luck for the lone hawthorn in a field.
senses.exampleCN: 老故事告诫人们，田里那株孤零零的山楂树会带来霉运。
senses.why: A single hawthorn standing apart in a field was often connected with fairies, so folklore treated the tree as a place of awe rather than ordinary timber.
senses.whyCN: 田里孤零零的一株山楂树常被与精灵联系起来，民俗便把它当作令人敬畏之地，而不是普通木料。

intro.en: Hawthorn joins the Old English word haga, a hedge or enclosed field, with thorn, the sharp spike; together they name the spiked bush that made the hedge.
intro.cn: hawthorn 由古英语的 haga（树篱、围起来的田）与 thorn（尖刺）组成，合起来指用来筑篱笆的多刺灌木。

items.en: The word is first recorded in this combined form, naming the thorny bush with its haws, the spikes that made a living hedge.
items.cn: 这个词最早以组合形式出现，用来指结山楂果、能把篱笆变成活墙的多刺灌木。

items.en: Spelling moves through forms like hawethorn and hauthorn while the simple word haw keeps the fruit sense alive beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语时期拼写经历 hawethorn、hauthorn 等变化，同时简短的 haw 一词继续保留「果实」的意思。

items.en: Botanical writers treat hawthorn as the name of a tree of the rose family, and its haws as a fruit gathered by country people.
items.cn: 十三世纪到十五世纪的植物学者把 hawthorn 当作蔷薇科一种树的名字，把它的山楂果视为乡间采摘的果实。

items.en: Enclosure planting makes the tree the standard hedge plant of the British countryside, and haythorn is an old spelling seen in some dialect sources.
items.cn: 圈地运动时期的栽种使它成为英国乡间标准的绿篱树种；在一些方言资料里还能见到旧拼写 haythorn。

items.en: Horticulture borrows the Chinese flowering species as ornamental plants, and the fruit of related species is sold worldwide as a tart, red health fruit.
items.cn: 现代园艺把原产中国的观赏品种引入园林，近缘种的果实也作为酸甜的红色保健果品销往世界各地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers plants and names that share the haw element or the thorn image; the near-meaning group gathers familiar thorny shrubs and trees from other families.
note.cn: 形近组汇集共享 haw 这一成分或同带荆棘意象的名称；近义组汇集来自其他科属、同样常见带刺的灌木与乔木。

entries.definition: The fruit of the hawthorn, the element that gives the tree the first half of its name.
entries.definitionCN: 山楂果，是本词前半部分的来源

entries.definition: The nut-bearing shrub, whose name is close in sound but not related; just spelling and sound alike, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 榛树，读音相近但词源无关，只是音近形近，词源不同

entries.definition: A fellow thorny hedge shrub that names itself after another word plus thorn, the same pattern this word follows.
entries.definitionCN: 同属绿篱的带刺灌木，按「另一个词 + thorn」的方式命名，本词也走同样的构词路子

entries.definition: A wild shrub with long arching stems and thorns, the other classic plant of a British hedge.
entries.definitionCN: 有长而弯垂的带刺茎的野生灌木，与山楂并称英国树篱里的典型植物

entries.definition: A thorn hedge grown from living cuttings, especially of hawthorn, laid to keep stock in.
entries.definitionCN: 用活的插条培育而成的带刺树篱，尤指山楂篱，用来拦住牲畜

entries.definition: A small, sour wild apple tree that blooms in the same spring hedgerow.
entries.definitionCN: 开在同一片春季树篱里、果实小而酸的野生苹果树

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real parts of the word, on the plants that grew beside it, and on the phrases the tree actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于这个词真实的构词成分、与它常相伴生长的植物，以及这种树实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: haw plus thorn: fruit first, spike second, and the thorny bush that carries the red haws is the hawthorn.
normal.cn: haw 加 thorn：先是果子，再是尖刺，挂着红果的多刺灌木就是 hawthorn。

normal.en: A hawthorn grows slowly and opens its white blossom in May, which is why old verses call it the May tree.
normal.cn: 山楂树长得慢，五月才开白花，老诗句因此叫它五月树。

normal.en: The same word gives blackthorn and whitetorn, and each names a hedge bush by the colour of its bark or blossom.
normal.cn: 同一个词还给出 blackthorn 与 whitetorn，各自按树皮或花的颜色给一种绿篱灌木命名。

normal.en: A hawthorn hedge is a boundary grown from soil, cut and laid each year so it stays dense and impassable.
normal.cn: hawthorn hedge 是从土里长出来的地界，每年修剪、编扎，使其保持密实、无法穿过。

normal.en: Its hard wood and spring flowers make hawthorn a favourite of hedgerows, and haythorn is an old spelling worth spotting.
normal.cn: 坚硬的木料与春天的花朵使山楂树成为绿篱的最爱；haythorn 是一个值得留意的旧拼写。

abstract.en: Picture a double row of white blossom in May, and lines of red berries hanging along the same thorny branches in autumn.
abstract.cn: 想象五月里两排雪白的山楂花，秋天同一根多刺的枝条上又挂满成串的红果。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole field edged by one dense hedge that stands in front of the wind and answers in thorns when a hand pushes it.
abstract.cn: 想象一整块田被一道密实的树篱围住，它挡在风前，人手一推就用荆棘回应。

abstract.en: Think of a single hawthorn standing alone in a meadow, and of walkers who step carefully around it because old stories hold it special.
abstract.cn: 想象一株孤零零立在草场上的山楂树，以及因为老故事而小心绕开它的行人。

examples.en: The hawthorn hedge along the lane shelters birds all winter.
examples.cn: 小路边的山楂树篱整个冬天都为鸟儿提供庇护。

examples.en: A row of hawthorns marks the boundary between the two farms.
examples.cn: 一排山楂树标示着两个农场之间的地界。

examples.en: She gathered hawthorn berries for a tart autumn preserve.
examples.cn: 她采了山楂果来做酸甜的秋日果酱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蒿刺」——蒿草丛里藏尖刺：hawthorn 就是多刺的灌木

root: 古英语 haga「树篱、围田」与 thorn「刺」合成本词；haga 与 haw（篱笆围地，即 haw 的本义）相关，由它演化出的 hedge 至今仍指树篱。整词的含义即「能筑成树篱的多刺灌木」，与果名 haw 在拼写上同挂一半。

sensesIntro.en: Hawthorn starts as the thorny tree itself, moves to its fruit and to the hedge it makes, and then widens into custom and folklore.
sensesIntro.cn: hawthorn 从多刺的树本身出发，继而指它的果实与它筑成的树篱，再延伸到节俗与民俗中的象征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small tree that flowers white in May, loads itself with red berries in autumn, and answers every hand that pushes it with a thorn.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵小而多刺的树，五月开白花，秋天挂满红果，谁去推它就扎谁。

branches.en: The tree is the core referent, named by the very two features that a woodland observer noticed: its thorns and its crop of haws.
branches.cn: 树本身是核心所指，命名时抓住的正是林中观察者最先注意到的两点：刺与山楂果。

branches.en: The fruit takes the name of the tree because it is the most visible thing the thorny bush produces each autumn.
branches.cn: 果实借用树名，因为它是这株多刺灌木每年秋天最显眼的东西。

branches.en: Field and hedge senses grow out of the planted rows, grown from the same thorny material that makes a fence.
branches.cn: 田界与树篱义由栽种的行列长出，这道「栅栏」正是用同样的多刺材料长成的。

branches.en: The blossom sense is set by the calendar rather than the shape of the plant, since white May flowers came to mark the start of summer.
branches.cn: 花季义由历法而非植株形态决定：五月的白花被用来标记入夏。

branches.en: The sacred sense is the tree as belief, drawn from loners in fields and from the thorn that seems to defend the spot.
branches.cn: 圣树义是树在信仰中的化身，源自田中孤株和那看似守护此地的荆棘。

intro.en: Hawthorn is a native English compound, so the pieces to learn are the stem haw, the familiar thorn, and the related words the two have grown.
intro.cn: hawthorn 是英语本土合成的复合词，要掌握的是词干 haw、常见的 thorn，以及二者各自长出的相关词。

latinIntro.en: The word itself has no Latin source; botanists later gave the genus a Latin name, and this word has no Latin cognates, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词本身没有拉丁语来源；植物学家后来给这一属取了拉丁学名，而这个词没有拉丁同源词，因此拉丁词页留空。

items.example: Haws are red, small and hard.
items.exampleCN: 山楂果小而红，质地很硬。

items.example: A lane lined with hawthorn is white in May.
items.exampleCN: 五月里两旁种着山楂树的小路一片雪白。

items.meaning: a sharp pointed growth on a plant
items.example: The hedgerow bristles with thorn.
items.exampleCN: 树篱上布满了刺。

items.meaning: a related thorny shrub with dark bark
items.example: Blackthorn sloes ripen in November.
items.exampleCN: 黑刺李的果实在十一月成熟。

items.example: Trim the hedge before winter.
items.exampleCN: 入冬前把树篱修剪一下。

items.example: Blackbirds strip the haws by midwinter.
items.exampleCN: 到了隆冬，乌鸦把山楂果吃得精光。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的（形容词后缀）
items.example: The suffix -y forms thorny and hawthorny.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 thorny 与 hawthorny。

items.example: A thorny problem is hard to handle.
items.exampleCN: thorny problem 指难以处理的问题。

items.meaning: having or wearing the thing named
items.example: The suffix -ed forms hawthorned.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 hawthorned。

items.example: Hawthorned lanes are a rural English sight.
items.exampleCN: 山楂夹道的小路是英国乡村一景。

definition_zh: 薄雾；烟雾；(思想或记忆的)模糊；使模糊
definition_en: thin mist, smoke or dust that hangs in the air and makes distant things look soft and unclear
core_image: 一层薄薄的灰白水汽罩在远处，景物边缘都糊成一片
scene: 清早的湖面浮着一层薄雾，对岸的树林只剩淡淡的轮廓。A thin haze covered the lake at dawn, and the far bank had blurred into a single grey shape.
sceneCN: 这里 haze 是「薄雾」（第 1 个义项：悬在空气中的薄雾，使远处景物模糊）；句意为清晨薄雾笼罩湖面，对岸的景物糊成了一片灰色。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「有薄雾的；模糊的」
由 hazy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「模糊地；朦胧地」
由 hazy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「朦胧；模糊不清」

senses.title: Thin mist in the air
senses.definition: a light mist of water vapour hanging in the air, thinner than fog and often softened by sunlight
senses.definitionCN: 悬在空气中的淡淡水汽，比雾更薄，常在阳光下显得柔和
senses.example: A morning haze hung over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的薄雾浮在山谷之上。
senses.why: The word names a thin airborne mist, the light veil that sunlight shows you most clearly when it falls across a distant hill.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指悬浮在空气中的薄薄水汽，是阳光斜照远山时最能被看见的那层轻纱。

senses.title: Smoke and pollution
senses.definition: a smoky or dusty film of polluted air, often over cities, forests and fire sites
senses.definitionCN: 烟尘弥漫或受污染的空气，常笼罩城市、林区与火场
senses.example: Exhaust from the traffic left a brown haze over the city.
senses.exampleCN: 交通废气在城市上空留下一层褐色的烟雾。
senses.why: Smoke and soot gathered in the same air produce an equally thin screen, so the word widened from water mist to smoke.
senses.whyCN: 烟与烟灰聚在同一片空气里，也能形成同样薄的屏障，于是这个词从水汽薄雾扩展到了烟。

senses.title: A blurred mind or memory
senses.definition: a confused or unclear state of the mind, of time, or of a memory
senses.definitionCN: 头脑、时间或记忆处于混乱、不清晰的状态
senses.example: The whole afternoon passed in a haze of fever.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午都在发烧的迷糊中过去了。
senses.why: A haze blurs the outlines of hills; by the same image, fatigue or fever blurs the outlines of thoughts.
senses.whyCN: 薄雾模糊山的轮廓；按同样的意象，疲惫或发烧也会模糊思绪的轮廓。

senses.title: To blur or obscure
senses.definition: to make something unclear, usually said of air, light or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 使事物变得不清晰，主语多为空气、光线或情绪
senses.example: Tears hazed her vision.
senses.exampleCN: 泪水让她的视线变得模糊。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the noun into an action: whatever acts like a hazy veil is said to haze what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词变成动作：凡是像薄纱一样起作用的东西，就被说成把后面的东西弄模糊了。

senses.title: Ritual humiliation
senses.titleCN: （校园或团体的）羞辱性入会仪式
senses.definition: a ritual in which newcomers to a group are treated with humiliating or physical ordeals
senses.definitionCN: 对新成员施以羞辱性或身体折磨的入会仪式
senses.example: The university now forbids hazing of new students in the dormitories.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学如今禁止在宿舍里对新来的学生搞羞辱性入会仪式。
senses.why: This sense is separate from the mist word; it comes from an old verb for making a man run a gauntlet of blows, and is a homonym rather than a development.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项与表示薄雾的词无关，来自古时让男人挨鞭跑的旧动词，是同形异源词，不是同一词的引申。

intro.en: Haze is a word of uncertain written origin. Its weather sense is first recorded in the late eighteenth century, and the connection some writers draw with the separate word for a horse is not established.
intro.cn: haze 的书面来源不确定。天气义的记录始于十八世纪后叶，有人把它与另一个表示马匹的同形词联系起来，但这种联系并未得到证实。

items.en: An older verb means to frighten or half-daze somebody, and a related use describes a horse; this material is the ground from which the later forms grew.
items.cn: 较早就有动词表示把某人吓住或弄迷糊，相关的用法还用来说马；后来的形式是从这些材料里长出来的。

items.en: Hazer and hazy appear in early texts, though the exact first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: hazer 与 hazy 见于早期文献，但二者确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun haze is first recorded with the weather sense of a thin cloud or mist, and writers link it to hazy.
items.cn: 名词 haze 最早以表示薄云薄雾的天气义被记录，作家们把它与 hazy 联系起来。

items.en: Coastal and regional use keeps the weather sense common, and the smoky urban haze of industrial towns joins it.
items.cn: 沿海与地方用法使天气义长期流行，工业城镇的烟霾又加入了这一义项。

items.en: The naming of a university ritual as hazing is the old verb for frightening and running a newcomer through blows, a homonym whose exact origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 把大学的入会仪式称为 hazing，源自表示吓唬并让新人挨打的旧动词，属于同形异源词，其确切来源不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words whose spelling sits one letter away from this one; the near-meaning group holds other words for mist and the states it blurs.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写只差一个字母的词；近义组收表示雾气及其模糊状态的其他词。

entries.definition: Actually related: the adjective made from haze, meaning misty or unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 确有关联：由 haze 加后缀构成的形容词，义为「有雾的；模糊的」

entries.definition: To look long and steadily; just spelling and sound alike, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间凝视，只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: To relax and do nothing at all; one opening letter apart in spelling only, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 懒散消磨时光，只是在拼写开头差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: A thin suspension of water droplets in the air, very close to haze though usually denser and closer to the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 悬在空气中的细小水滴，与薄雾极近，但通常更浓、更贴近地面

entries.definition: A thick cloud at ground level that can cut visibility hard, heavier than a haze.
entries.definitionCN: 贴地而浓密的云，能大幅降低能见度，比薄雾浓重

entries.definition: Polluted fog that blends smoke and mist, the urban cousin of a smoky haze.
entries.definitionCN: 烟与雾混合的空气污染，是烟霾在城市里的近亲

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the words haze actually grew with, the phrases it appears in, and the plain spellings that sit beside it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用上 haze 真正生长出来的词、它出现的短语，以及紧挨着它的一些普通拼写。

normal.en: The adjective hazy is a simple change of z to y, and it names the very look that a thin mist gives a hill.
normal.cn: 形容词 hazy 只是把 z 换成 y，它命名的正是薄雾给山头带来的那种样子。

normal.en: Mist, fog and smog sit near this word, and they measure the same veil from thin to thick.
normal.cn: mist、fog 与 smog 与这个词相邻，它们把同一层纱从薄到厚排列出来。

normal.en: Heat haze is the shimmering air above a hot road, the most familiar form of the thin screen.
normal.cn: heat haze 是炽热路面上方颤抖的空气，是这层薄纱最常见的形式。

normal.en: A morning haze usually clears by noon, so the word carries a hint of something brief.
normal.cn: morning haze 通常在正午前散去，所以这个词带着「短暂」的暗示。

normal.en: Remember the homonym rule: the mist word and the hazing verb share letters but not history.
normal.cn: 记住同形词的规则：表示薄雾的词与表示羞辱仪式的动词共拼写，但不共历史。

abstract.en: Picture a row of soft grey hills, each one paler than the one before, and know that the pale hand between them is the haze.
abstract.cn: 想象一排柔和灰绿的山，一座比一座淡，明白它们之间那只把颜色冲淡的手就是 haze。

abstract.en: Imagine a wedding veil thrown over a town at dawn and lifted again by nine o clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一条薄纱黎明时罩在城镇上空，到九点又被掀开。

abstract.en: Think of a thought you cannot quite catch, seen through the same thin grey film as the hills.
abstract.cn: 想一件你怎么也抓不住的念头，它像山一样隔着同一层淡灰的膜。

examples.en: The haze lifted and the mountains stood out sharply.
examples.cn: 薄雾散去，群山一下子清晰起来。

examples.en: A faint haze of dust hung in the afternoon air.
examples.cn: 午后空气中浮着一层淡淡的尘雾。

examples.en: Thick haze from the forest fire spread over the town for days.
examples.cn: 林火的浓烟在城市上空弥漫了好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨」——满街嗨声被雾糊成一团：hei 声里的 h 变成了 haze

root: 词源不确定：最早见于十六世纪的 hazer 与 hazy，名词天气义到十八世纪后叶才出现。学界一般认为与古时表示「吓唬、使迷糊」的动词同源，因此有「把人弄迷糊」→「空气让人看不清」的联想，但这一推导并未定论；表示马匹与校园仪式的用法属于同形异源词。

sensesIntro.en: Haze begins as thin mist, widens to smoke and polluted air, then turns inward to a blurred mind, and finally becomes a verb and a word of another origin.
sensesIntro.cn: haze 从薄雾起头，扩展到烟与受污染的空气，再转向内在模糊的头脑，最后既变成动词，也出现一个来源不同的同形词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin grey veil of water vapour lying over a lake, with the far bank turning into a single soft shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄薄的灰白水汽铺在湖面上，对岸化成一片柔和模糊的轮廓。

branches.en: The core weather sense keeps the veil as vapour only, thin enough for sunlight to shine through.
branches.cn: 核心天气义只把纱当作水汽，薄得足以让阳光穿过。

branches.en: Smoke and soot take the place of water droplets but keep the same optical effect, so the veil widens to pollution.
branches.cn: 烟与烟灰取代了水滴，却保留同样的光学效果，纱因此扩展为污染的空气。

branches.en: The blurred outline seen in the air is transferred to the blurred outline of thoughts, from foggy weather to a foggy mind.
branches.cn: 空中模糊的轮廓被移用到思绪的轮廓上，于是从雾天走到迷糊的头脑。

branches.en: The verb carries the noun into action as whatever veils a thing onto the thing it veils.
branches.cn: 动词把名词推进动作，主语变作那层遮蔽之物，宾语变作被遮的东西。

branches.en: The hazing or ritual sense is a separate word that happens to look identical, and it must be learned apart.
branches.cn: 入会仪式义只是碰巧长得一模一样的另一个词，须单独记忆。

intro.en: Haze is a short English word of uncertain origin, so what is worth learning is its small family, its common partners and the words that merely share its shape.
intro.cn: haze 是个来源不确定的英语短词，值得学习的是它的小词族、常见搭配，以及那些仅仅长得相似的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for this word, and no Latin cousins are established for it, so this Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖形，也未能确认拉丁同源词，因此拉丁词页留空。

items.example: A haze softened the afternoon sun.
items.exampleCN: 薄雾让午后的阳光变得柔和。

items.example: The far coast was hazy.
items.exampleCN: 远处的海岸雾蒙蒙的。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的（形容词后缀）
items.example: The suffix -y turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词。

items.meaning: in an unclear or misty way
items.example: The lights shone hazily through the mist.
items.exampleCN: 灯光穿过雾气朦胧地亮着。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms adverbs from adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Haziness in photos comes from stray light.
items.exampleCN: 照片的朦胧感来自杂散光。

items.example: The suffix -ness names a quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 为一种性质命名。

items.meaning: more than one haze; also the third person of the verb
items.meaningCN: 复数形式；也用于动词第三人称单数
items.example: Thick hazes settle over the delta each year.
items.exampleCN: 每年都有浓烟沉降在这片三角洲上。

items.meaning: past tense and past participle of the verb
items.meaningCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词
items.example: The glass was hazed with steam.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃被蒸汽弄得模糊了。

items.meaning: a ritual of humiliation; also the continuing form of the verb
items.meaningCN: 羞辱性入会仪式；也作动词现在分词
items.example: Hazing is banned by many colleges now.
items.exampleCN: 如今许多大学禁止羞辱性入会仪式。

definition_zh: 校长（尤指英国私立学校的男校长）
definition_en: the man in charge of a school, especially a private school in Britain
core_image: 一位站在校门前、手扶帽檐的校长，胸前别着校徽
scene: 毕业典礼上，校长把证书一个个递到学生手里。At the end of term the headmaster stood by the gate and shook hands with every pupil.
sceneCN: 这里 headmaster 是「校长」（第 1 个义项：负责一所学校的男性校长，尤指英国的私立学校）；句意为学期结束时校长站在校门口，与每一位学生握手。

pos.zh: 校长（尤指英国私立学校的男校长）

derivatives.zh: 由 head 加 mistress 构成，指女校长，与 headmaster 成对使用
由 master 加名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「主持；统治」，与校长职务共享同一词根
由 master 加名词后缀 -y 构成，义为「精通；支配」，反映 master 一词「掌握者」的本义

senses.title: The male head of a school
senses.titleCN: 男校长（尤指英国私立学校）
senses.definition: the man who is in charge of a school, used especially of a private or independent school in Britain
senses.definitionCN: 负责一所学校事务的男性，尤用于英国的私立学校
senses.example: The headmaster announced that the school would open a new science block.
senses.exampleCN: 校长宣布学校将新建一座科学楼。
senses.why: The compound puts the Old English head, meaning the top or the chief, in front of the Latin master, meaning one with authority, so the word simply names the man at the head of the masters.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把古英语里表示「顶端、首领」的 head 放在表示「有权力者」的拉丁语 master 前面，字面上就是「教师们之首」。

senses.title: A traditional public-school leader kind of figure
senses.definition: the image of a stern authority figure shaped by old British public schools and boys boarding schools
senses.definitionCN: 由英国老牌公学与男子寄宿学校塑造出的严厉权威形象
senses.example: In many novels the headmaster is stern, formal and fond of long speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多小说里，校长严厉、拘礼，还爱长篇讲话。
senses.why: Because British boys schools long used the title exclusively, literature turned it into a stock figure of authority and ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 由于英国男子学校长期专用这一头衔，文学便把它塑造成权威与仪式的固定形象。

senses.title: The senior master in a college
senses.definition: a senior teacher who leads a college, a house or a department in some older schools
senses.definitionCN: 在一些老式学校里负责一个学院、宿舍或系科的资深教师
senses.example: As headmaster of the old hall, he kept the library in order.
senses.exampleCN: 身为老学堂的院长，他把图书馆管理得井井有条。
senses.why: In older schools the head of a college or hall also carried the title, so the word once stretched beyond a single school building.
senses.whyCN: 在老式学校里，负责学院或学堂的人也用这个头衔，所以这个词一度超出单单一栋校舍的范围。

senses.title: The head of an informal or imagined school
senses.definition: a jokey extension of the school title to anyone who runs a group, club or household
senses.definitionCN: 把学校头衔戏谑地扩用到主持小组、俱乐部或家庭的任何人
senses.example: My sister calls herself the headmaster of our kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我妹妹自称是我们厨房的校长。
senses.why: The word survives in everyday speech as a light joke, where any household or club leader is dressed up in the old school title.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在日常口语里作为轻松的玩笑留存下来，任何家庭或俱乐部的主事者都被套上这身老校装束。

intro.en: Headmaster joins two words from different centuries: the Old English head, a chief or top, and the Latin master, a person with authority, which reached English through Latin and Old French.
intro.cn: headmaster 把两个不同世纪来源的词接在一起：古英语里表示「首领、顶端」的 head，以及表示「有权力者」的拉丁语 master，后者经拉丁语与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Magister means one who has authority, a chief, a teacher, and maior means greater; both come from magis, more, and metior, to measure.
items.cn: magister 意为有权力者、首领、教师，maior 意为更大的；二者都源自 magis（更多）与 metior（衡量）。

items.en: Maistre carries the word into English, where master steadily covers a teacher and a man in charge.
items.cn: maistre 把这个词带入英语，master 逐渐兼指教师与负责人。

items.en: Heafod means the head of a body and also a chief or top, the source of modern head.
items.cn: heafod 既指身体的头，也指首领或顶端，是现代英语 head 的来源。

items.en: Headmaster is recorded meaning the head of a school or college in the sixteenth century, though the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: headmaster 在十六世纪已有「学校或学院之长」的记录，但确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: The title is strongly fixed to British boys schools, and headmistress is coined beside it for girls schools.
items.cn: 这一头衔牢固地挂靠到英国男子学校上，与之相对，女子学校另创 headmistress 一词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the head stem or the master stem; the near-meaning group gathers titles men and women hold when they run a school.
note.cn: 形近组汇集共享 head 词干或 master 词干的词；近义组汇集男女主持校务时所用的各种头衔。

entries.definition: The paired title for a woman who runs a school, formed with mistress in place of master.
entries.definitionCN: 与 headmaster 配对的头衔，用 mistress 取代 master，指负责学校的女性

entries.definition: A title for a teacher or a man with authority, the second half of this compound.
entries.definitionCN: 对教师或有权力者的称呼，是本词的后半部分

entries.definition: A great conductor or master of an art; related in root but borrowed through Italian, and often confused with master by spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 杰出的指挥或艺术大师；词根相关却经意大利语借入，常因拼写与 master 混淆

entries.definition: The head of a school used mostly in North America and in some other systems.
entries.definitionCN: 校长的称呼，多用于北美及其他一些教育体系

entries.definition: The neutral, modern British title for the leader of a school.
entries.definitionCN: 英国现代较中性的称呼，指学校的领导者

entries.definition: A title for the head of some schools, colleges and churches, chiefly in older British and Scottish use.
entries.definitionCN: 某些学校、学院与教会的负责人头衔，多见于英国与苏格兰的旧用法

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the word, its British school setting, and the titles that grew up beside it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用上这个词真实的两半、它在英国学校的语境，以及围绕它长出的各种头衔。

normal.en: Head plus master: the man at the head of all the masters, the chief of the teachers.
normal.cn: head 加 master：站在所有 masters 最前面的那个人，也就是教师中的首席。

normal.en: Headmaster and headmistress are a matched pair, and British schools long chose one or the other by the sex of the pupils.
normal.cn: headmaster 与 headmistress 是一对，英国学校长期按学生的性别选用其中一个。

normal.en: In Britain a headteacher or head runs a state school, while headmaster keeps an older, private school flavour.
normal.cn: 在英国，headteacher 或 head 负责公立学校，headmaster 则保留一种老式私立学校的味道。

normal.en: Do not confuse the stem master with the Italian-like maestro, which names a great artist or conductor.
normal.cn: 不要把词干 master 与类似意大利语的 maestro 混淆，后者指杰出的艺术家或指挥。

normal.en: An assistant headmaster is a deputy, so the head remains the one at the very top.
normal.cn: assistant headmaster 是副职，可见 head 仍是站在最高处的那一个。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor of classroom doors, and one man standing at the far end facing all of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一条挂满教室门的走廊，尽头有一个人面对所有教室门站着。

abstract.en: Imagine a speech on the first day of term, delivered from a small stage with the whole school seated below.
abstract.cn: 想象开学第一天的讲话，从一个小讲台上讲出，全校学生坐在下面。

abstract.en: Think of a brass name plate over an office door, polished each year by whoever holds the post.
abstract.cn: 想象办公室门上的一块铜牌，年年由在任者擦亮。

examples.en: The headmaster gave a short speech at the ceremony.
examples.cn: 校长在典礼上简短致辞。

examples.en: He served as headmaster of the school for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他担任这所学校的校长达二十年。

examples.en: The new headmaster promised more support for music lessons.
examples.cn: 新校长承诺为音乐课提供更多支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑马斯特」——骑黑马的人站在校门口：headmaster 就是校长

root: 由古英语 heafod（头、首领，现代 head）与经古法语传入的拉丁语 magister（有权力者、教师，现代 master）合成，字面义「教师之首」；magister 又出自 magis「更多」与 metior「衡量」，指地位更高、更受衡量者。

sensesIntro.en: Headmaster begins as the male head of a school, is fixed to the traditional British school image, opens to a senior college leader, and finally turns into a joking title.
sensesIntro.cn: headmaster 先指负责学校的男性，后被固定在传统英国学校的形象上，再扩展到学院里的高级教师，最后变成戏谑的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man at the head of a line of teachers, standing before the school gate with the badge of the school on his coat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名男子站在教师队伍最前方，在校门口站着，大衣上别着校徽。

branches.en: The compound sense keeps both halves in view: the head of a body of masters, in charge of the whole school.
branches.cn: 复合义保留两半的面貌：教师群体的头，掌管整所学校。

branches.en: Literature and long custom give this title a flavour of ceremony and discipline tied to boys boarding schools.
branches.cn: 文学与长期习惯让这一头衔带上寄宿男校的仪式感与纪律色彩。

branches.en: Where a college wanted a senior teacher in charge, the same two halves were ready to name that role too.
branches.cn: 学院需要一位资深教师负责时，同样的两半也可用来命名这一职务。

branches.en: The joking use keeps the school title but drops the school, turning any group leader into a mock headmaster.
branches.cn: 戏谑用法保留学校头衔却丢掉学校，把任何带头人都变成拍脑袋的校长。

branches.en: The central title and the public-school image feed each other: the school head is the figure that novels and ceremonies turn into a symbol of authority.
branches.cn: 核心头衔与公学形象相互助长：正是学校之长这一角色，被小说与典礼塑造成权威的象征。

intro.en: Headmaster is a compound of a native Old English word and a Latin borrowing, so the pieces worth learning are head, master and the family both have grown.
intro.cn: headmaster 是本土古英语词与拉丁借词的合成词，值得学习的是 head、master 以及两者各自长出的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin master behind this word is magister, a noun of authority from magis and maior, and that single root feeds master, mastery, masterful and more.
latinIntro.cn: 本词背后的拉丁语 master 是 magister，一个表示权威的名词，源出 magis 与 maior，这一个词根还生出 master、mastery、masterful 等词。

items.example: Head is the native half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: head 是这个复合词的本土一半。

items.example: A master teaches and rules.
items.exampleCN: master 既教课也掌事。

items.meaning: the male head of a school
items.example: The headmaster rang the bell for assembly.
items.exampleCN: 校长敲响了集会的钟。

items.example: The suffix -ess forms headmistress.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ess 构成 headmistress。

items.meaning: the female head of a school
items.example: She was the first headmistress of the school.
items.exampleCN: 她是这所学校的第一位女校长。

items.meaningCN: 表示职位或状态的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ship forms mastership.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ship 构成 mastership。

items.example: He took up the mastership in September.
items.exampleCN: 他在九月就任这一主持之职。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或技能的后缀
items.example: The suffix -y forms mastery.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 mastery。

items.example: Mastery of grammar takes years.
items.exampleCN: 精通语法需要多年。

items.example: A masterful performance won the prize.
items.exampleCN: 一场技艺高超的演出拿下了奖项。

definition_zh: 把总部设在；设总部于；以……为总部
definition_en: to establish or have your main office or control centre in a particular place
core_image: 一个大脑袋坐在棋盘正中央，所有线路都往这里收拢
scene: 这家公司把总部设在小城，因为大学就在附近。The company decided to headquarter its offices in a smaller city close to the university.
sceneCN: 这里 headquarter 是动词「设总部于」（第 1 个义项：把总部设在某地）；句意：这家公司决定把办公总部设在一座靠近大学的小城里。

pos.zh: 总部；司令部（兼作 headquarters 的单数拼写，多用复数形式）

collocations.zh: 把业务指挥中心设在此处

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复数词尾构成，义为「总部；司令部」；单数直接写 headquarters
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「总部设于……的」
由现在分词转作名词，义为「设总部；总部选址」

senses.title: To place the main office in a place
senses.definition: to make a particular place the site of your main office and decision-making centre
senses.definitionCN: 把某个地方确定为主办公室与决策中心的所在地
senses.example: They plan to headquarter the new firm in Leeds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打算把新公司总部设在利兹。
senses.why: The base headquarters names the main office, and the verb moves it onto a place: to headquarter is to put the head there.
senses.whyCN: 名词 headquarters 指「主办公室」，动词则把这个「头」安放出去：headquarter 就是把指挥机构放到某地。

senses.title: To have your main office somewhere
senses.definition: to be based in a place, used mainly in the passive with the company as the subject
senses.definitionCN: 把某地作为基地，主要用于被动语态，主语为公司等机构
senses.example: The start-up is headquartered in Osaka.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司以大阪为总部。
senses.why: When the focus shifts from the place to the body based there, the passive turns the verb into a label of location.
senses.whyCN: 当视角从地点转到设在那里的机构时，被动式就把这个动词变成了「总部所在地」的标签。

senses.title: To supply headquarters for a unit
senses.titleCN: 为……设立司令部；设立指挥机构
senses.definition: to set up the central command post for a military unit or an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 为军事部队或组织设立中央指挥机构
senses.example: The colonel was ordered to headquarter the unit near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 上校奉命把部队的司令部设在海边。
senses.why: The military use came before the business use: a headquarters was first a command post, so the verb meant providing one.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法早于商业用法：「总部」最初是司令部，所以动词先表示设立指挥机构。

intro.en: Headquarter is a back-formation from headquarters, itself a compound of head and quarters meaning lodgings.
intro.cn: headquarter 是由 headquarters 逆构而来的动词，headquarters 本身是 head（头）与 quarters（住所）的复合词。

items.en: Heafod means the head, the top or the chief part.
items.cn: heafod 意为头、顶部或首要部分。

items.en: Quartier means a quarter or the fourth part of a place.
items.cn: quartier 意为一块区域或某地的四分之一。

items.en: Quarters comes to mean lodgings or the place where troops are stationed.
items.cn: quarters 转而表示营房，或部队驻扎之处。

items.en: Headquarters forms as the compound of head and quarters for a commander and staff.
items.cn: headquarters 由 head 与 quarters 复合而成，指指挥官与参谋所在的驻地。

items.en: Businesses borrow the military word for their central office.
items.cn: 商业机构借用这个军事词来指自己的中央办公室。

items.en: The verb headquarter is back-formed from the plural noun, first for troops and later for firms.
items.cn: 动词 headquarter 从复数名词逆构而来，先用于军队，后用于公司。

note.en: Headquarter is the verb built from headquarters, so it sits beside base, locate and head office words, and is easily confused with head and quarter.
note.cn: headquarter 是从 headquarters 构造出的动词，因此与 base、locate 等「设置」动词及「总部」类词相邻，也容易和 head、quarter 混淆。

entries.definition: the main office or command centre of an organisation
entries.definitionCN: 总部；司令部（本词的来源名词）

entries.definition: the top or leading part of something
entries.definitionCN: 头；首脑；领导（构成 headquarters 的第一部分）

entries.definition: a district, or a place to stay
entries.definitionCN: 地区；住处（构成 quarters 的第二部分）

entries.definition: to have or place something in a particular place
entries.definitionCN: 以……为基地；把……设在

entries.definition: to put something in a particular position
entries.definitionCN: 把……设置在（某处）

entries.definition: to place a firm or office in a place
entries.definitionCN: 把公司或办事处设立在某地

normalIntro.en: Headquarter is built from head plus quarters, so remember the image of moving the brain of an organisation into a building.
normalIntro.cn: headquarter 由 head 与 quarters 构成，记住的画面是：把一个机构的「大脑」搬进某栋楼里。

normal.en: Headquarter is a back-formation from headquarters.
normal.cn: headquarter 是从 headquarters 逆构出来的动词。

normal.en: Head plus quarters means the chief place where staff are lodged.
normal.cn: head 加 quarters 指人员安顿的首要去处。

normal.en: The pattern be headquartered in answers where a firm is based.
normal.cn: be headquartered in 这一结构回答公司的基地在哪里。

normal.en: Both spellings end in s in the noun, because headquarters treats the office as plural.
normal.cn: 名词两种写法都以 s 结尾，因为 headquarters 把办公机构看作复数实体。

normal.en: Compare base and locate: headquarter is narrower and only fits institutions.
normal.cn: 对比 base 与 locate：headquarter 更窄，只适用于机构。

abstract.en: Picture a chessboard with a giant head sitting on the middle square.
abstract.cn: 想象棋盘正中央坐着一颗巨大的头。

abstract.en: Imagine many arrows arriving from all over a map into one building.
abstract.cn: 想象地图四面八方的箭头都指向同一栋楼。

abstract.en: Think of a company moving into a new building and putting up its name.
abstract.cn: 想象公司搬进新楼，在门口挂起自己的招牌。

examples.en: The airline is headquartered in Dublin and flies to over one hundred cities.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司总部设在都柏林，航线通向一百多个城市。

examples.en: They chose to headquarter the research team on the same campus as the hospital.
examples.cn: 他们选择把研究团队的总部设在医院同一个园区里。

examples.en: For tax reasons, several shipping firms decided to headquarter their offices abroad.
examples.cn: 出于税务原因，几家航运公司决定把办公总部设在海外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑的跨特」——把「头儿」跨过街道搬进新的街区，就是设总部；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 heafod（头、首要部分）+ 古法语 quartier（区域）→ 中古英语 quarters（营房）→ 复合词 headquarters（司令部）→ 逆构动词 headquarter，核心义「把指挥中枢放到某处」。

sensesIntro.en: Headquarter moves from placing the main office, to the passive label of where a firm is based, to the older military act of setting up a command post.
sensesIntro.cn: headquarter 的义项从「把主办公室设在某地」，到被动式「以某地为总部」，再到较早的军事义「设立司令部」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large head is seated on the middle square of a board, and every line runs towards it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗大头坐在棋盘正中央，所有线路都向它收拢。

branches.en: The act sense: the verb moves the head office into a chosen place.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词把主办公室放进选定的地点。

branches.en: The location sense: the passive says where the organisation keeps its head.
branches.cn: 位置线：被动式说明机构把「头」安放在哪里。

branches.en: The military sense: the earliest use sets up a command post for troops.
branches.cn: 军事线：最早的用法是为部队设立指挥所。

branches.en: Naming the site and stating the site are two views of the same move of the head office.
branches.cn: 指明选址与陈述所在地，是主办公室同一迁移行为的两个视角。

branches.en: Both senses keep the head plus quarters image, one for a firm and one for an army.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留 head 加 quarters 的意象，一个用于公司，一个用于军队。

intro.en: Headquarter is a compound with an English head and a French-derived quarters, plus suffixes built on the noun.
intro.cn: headquarter 是一个复合词，由英语的 head 与源自法语的 quarters 组成，再借后缀扩展出名词与分词形式。

latinIntro.en: The first element descends from early Germanic forms, not Latin, while quarters goes back through French to Latin quartarius, so only the lower layer is Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 第一部分源自早期日耳曼语而非拉丁语，quarters 则经法语上溯到拉丁语 quartarius，因此只有底层部分属于拉丁语。

items.example: Head marks the leading part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: head 标示复合词中「首要」的一端。

items.example: Quarters supplies the place sense.
items.exampleCN: quarters 提供「地点」这一含义。

items.example: The compound ends the family as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合名词充当词族的名词终点。

items.example: The suffix makes headquarters look plural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾让 headquarters 看起来像复数。

items.meaningCN: 过去分词与形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix forms headquartered.
items.exampleCN: -ed 构成 headquartered。

items.example: Headquartered usually follows the verb be.
items.exampleCN: headquartered 通常放在 be 动词之后。

items.meaningCN: 现在分词或动作名词词尾
items.example: The suffix forms headquartering.
items.exampleCN: -ing 构成 headquartering。

items.meaning: the main office of a firm
items.example: Head office is the everyday paraphrase of headquarters.
items.exampleCN: head office 是 headquarters 的日常同义说法。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 四分之一的；四分之一量

definition_zh: 头戴式耳机；耳麦；虚拟现实头显；语音通信器件
definition_en: a device worn on the head that carries sound to the ears, often with a microphone for speaking
core_image: 一副耳机连同话筒从头顶套下，把嘴巴和耳朵一起罩住
scene: 客服戴上耳麦，一边听你说话，一边在键盘上敲字。The call centre agent put on a headset so that her hands stayed free for the keyboard.
sceneCN: 这里 headset 是「耳麦」（第 2 个义项：带话筒、双手可空出来的通话耳机）；句意：客服戴上一副耳麦来听你讲话，双手就能空出来敲键盘。

pos.zh: （旧）头戴式听话器；头部佩戴装置

derivatives.zh: 由 head 与 phone 复合而成，义为「头戴式耳机」，与本词常互换
由 head 与 gear 复合而成，义为「头饰；头部装备」
由 hand 替换 head 构成的同构复合词，义为「电话手柄；手机」

senses.title: Sound device worn on the head
senses.definition: a pair of headphones fitted over the head, held in place by a band
senses.definitionCN: 罩在头上、用横梁固定的双耳耳机
senses.example: She packed her headset for the long flight.
senses.exampleCN: 她为长途飞行带上了头戴式耳机。
senses.why: Head names the place of wearing and set names the outfit, so a headset is literally a set for the head.
senses.whyCN: head 标明佩戴的部位，set 指成套的器具，所以 headset 字面就是「给头部用的一整套东西」。

senses.title: Earpiece and microphone for calls
senses.definition: a headphone unit with a microphone attached, used for telephone or online calls
senses.definitionCN: 附有话筒的耳机组件，用于电话或网络通话
senses.example: Support staff wear headsets all day.
senses.exampleCN: 客服人员全天都戴着耳麦。
senses.why: Once a microphone joins the set, the device handles both listening and talking, so the word marks a complete communication kit.
senses.whyCN: 加上话筒后，这套器具既能听也能说，于是这个词就指一整套通话设备。

senses.title: Display worn over the eyes
senses.definition: a head-worn display that shows computer images, as used in virtual or augmented reality
senses.definitionCN: 戴在头上、显示计算机画面的装置，用于虚拟现实或增强现实
senses.example: The new headset shows a game in three dimensions.
senses.exampleCN: 新的头显能以三维画面显示游戏。
senses.why: The set no longer carries only sound; whatever is strapped to the head keeps the name, so the display borrows headset.
senses.whyCN: 这套器具不再只承载声音：凡绑在头上的装置都沿用这个名字，于是头戴显示器也借用了 headset。

senses.title: Old term for a telephone earpiece
senses.definition: an early device that held a single receiver to the ear for listening to a message
senses.definitionCN: 早期把单个听筒固定在耳边以便听讯息的装置
senses.example: Telegraph clerks were issued a headset and a small microphone.
senses.exampleCN: 电报员各配了一副耳机听话器和小话筒。
senses.why: In the telegraph age the set was minimal, only a receiver on a spring band, yet the naming pattern was the same.
senses.whyCN: 在电报时代，这套器具极其简单，只是弹性带上的一个听筒，但命名思路完全一样。

intro.en: Headset is a modern English compound of head and set, formed in the age of the telephone and the radio.
intro.cn: headset 是现代英语的复合词，由 head 与 set 组合而成，产生于电话与无线电普及的年代。

items.en: Heafod names the head.
items.cn: heafod 指头。

items.en: Settan means to set or place something down.
items.cn: settan 意为把某物放下或放置。

items.en: Set develops the noun sense of a group or collection of things.
items.cn: set 发展出名词义「一组、一套物品」。

items.en: Telegraph and telephone work creates the need for gear worn on the head.
